quote: Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go in to them, and I will praise the Lord.
body: Heavenly Father, as this day opens we pause to bring our lives into step with your good purposes — it’s foolish, we know, to fight against what you’re doing. Give us wisdom, a heart tuned to your voice, a clearer sense of what we owe each other, and the peace that comes from working alongside you rather than against you. Extend all of this to everyone we love. Make your love and your ways known everywhere, until all people live together in peace under your care. We ask this through Jesus, your Son and our Redeemer. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Russell H. Conwell, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: His love is perfected in us.
body: Heavenly Father, write your name — Love — on our hearts this morning. Help us keep Jesus close through the busy hours, so that whenever our minds are free they turn to him instead of drifting. Keep us from wounding him by careless thought or word. Forgive us for the empty promises we’ve made and the ways we’ve blurred the line between your church and the world. Save us from despair; light hope in every heart. Remind us that broken lives can be rebuilt, and that Christ is enough for whatever we need. Wash away the memory of our wandering, and let us know the joy of being called your children. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Frederick T. Keeney, D.D., Syracuse, N.Y.

quote: Make his praise glorious.
body: Gracious God, we look to you for your blessing. We are your dependent children, living only by your patience, grateful for mercies beyond counting. You made us for relationship — with you and with each other — so let that friendship with you be the foundation of everything else. Teach us how to be humbled and how to flourish. Comfort us when tears come, and turn our long nights of sorrow into joyful mornings. Let this life be a preview of the eternal home you’ve built for us. Help us remember you even in our simple pleasures, and bring us at last, joyful and unafraid, into your presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles F. Wishart, D.D., Chicago, Illinois.

quote: Keep yourselves in the love of God.
body: Eternal Love, whom Jesus taught us to call Father — and to trust as brother, companion, closest friend — we’re not searching for you, because we know you’re already nearer to us than we are to ourselves. We simply hope that today, again and again, the thought of your presence will rise up in us: that we’ll see what you’re showing us, hear what you’re telling us, and be ready to receive and to do what you ask. Let us recognize the good thoughts and kind impulses in our hearts as signs of you living there. Help us to work alongside you, today and every day, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Washington Gladden, D.D., LL.D., Columbus, Ohio.

quote: O Lord, my God, I will give thanks unto thee forever.
body: Eternal Father, thank you for bringing us close as your children through the death of Jesus Christ, your Son, through whom we’re adopted into your family. Thank you for sharing not only our sorrows but our joys, and for delighting when goodness and faithfulness lift us higher. Thank you for your Word — may our study of it bring real growth, so that we never begin a day without its nourishment. Bless everyone dear to us, and let our friendships be shaped by our friendship with Christ. We ask it in his holy name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John Timothy Stone, D.D., Chicago, Illinois.

quote: I thank thee and praise thee, O God.
body: Our Father in heaven, we come to you through Jesus Christ to give thanks, to ask forgiveness for our sins, and to seek your Spirit’s guidance in every choice and every act of service. We know how short our sight is, how flawed our judgment, how weak our efforts — but you’ve promised that if we commit our way to you and trust you, you’ll see it through. Give us sympathetic hearts, kind faces, generous words, and helping hands, so we can be a channel of blessing like Abraham was. Give us strength for what’s right in front of us today, through Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by J. A. Duff, D.D., Aspinwall, Pa.

quote: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us.
body: In you, God, we live and move and exist — if you withdrew your hand even for a moment, we’d vanish like dew in the air. Thank you for everything that makes life worth living: home, family, true friends, the hope of doing good, and the promise of life beyond this one, revealed in the gospel. Forgive our sins for Jesus’ sake, so we’re not dragging around a hopeless burden. Make us generous toward everyone we can help, and look kindly on the sick and suffering. Hear us — not because we deserve it, but because we ask in Christ’s name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by David J. Burrell, D.D., New York City.

quote: I will love thee, O Lord, my strength.
body: Almighty God, creator and keeper of all things, we bow before you with nothing to offer except that we’ve been redeemed through the suffering, death, and resurrection of your only Son, Jesus Christ. Thank you for all you’ve given us; give us the wisdom to become a blessing to everyone we meet. Forgive our sins. Walk with us today — be our friend, our counselor, our guide, the staff we lean on — so that love for you and for others fills our lives and shows in everything we do. You haven’t promised to give us everything we want, but you have promised to meet every need; grant us contentment with what you provide. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by William Anthony Granville, LL.D., Gettysburg, Pa.

quote: Give thanks unto the Lord, call upon his name.
body: Dear Heavenly Father, as we gather as a family today, we ask your blessing on our home and your guidance through every hour ahead. Help us feel how near you really are — not a distant King ruling from far off, but a Savior and Friend closer than our dearest companions. Let us hear your voice today, feel the lift of your presence, and walk gladly wherever your light falls. Give us some work to do for others, a kind word to say, some small unselfish act to offer in your name — so that your will is done, and your kingdom comes, right in our hearts. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Mrs. Maud Ballington Booth, New York City.

quote: I will bless the Lord at all times.
body: Lord and Father of us all, we come gladly to this hour of prayer. Your power, wisdom, and goodness leave us in awe, and we choose you as our example — let your Spirit reshape us into your likeness. As parents, help us raise our children wisely, for lives of purpose here and a true home beyond. Keep our closeness as a family from turning into friction; make us gentle with one another. We pray for everyone in trouble — the sick, the poor, the lonely — that they’d find comfort and companionship in you. Thank you for every good gift, freely given. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles Randall Barnes, D.D., Hoboken, N.J.

quote: Hear, and in thy faithfulness answer me.
body: Our Father, our hearts overflow with gratitude when we count your mercies, and we feel how little we deserve any of your kindness — yet bear with us patiently. Free us from selfish, lesser desires, and let us give you the love and service that’s rightfully yours. Don’t let us work against you or apart from you, but let us share in your purposes and your joy. Forgive our doubts and our weak faith; when mountains of difficulty rise ahead, give us faith enough to move them. Help us live forgetful of self, and lead us by your Spirit into the fullness of your life within us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Justin N. Green, Cincinnati, Ohio.

quote: The faithful God, which keepeth covenant.
body: Heavenly Father, we thank you for your endless mercies and ask your protection over every step we take. Grant us grace to please you in all we think, plan, and do, and let us live in such closeness with you that you can work through us, not just dwell in us. Help us share our blessings and see our privileges as a call to serve others. Give us strength for our work, courage in fear, comfort in sorrow, and peace beyond understanding. Watch over everyone we love, and let us take joy in seeing your kingdom advance, in Christ’s name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by James I. Vance, D.D., Nashville, Tenn.

quote: If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God, and he will give it him.
body: Infinite Father, we’ve tried the world and found it empty; we come back to you, the source of truth and mercy, with a song in our hearts, for your gifts to us are beyond counting. Thank you for the challenges of today, full of chances to help others, and for the unknown days ahead, however they come. Thank you for the quiet heroism of home life and the small sacrifices no one sees. Even though we so often get in our own way and wander from Christ’s path, we come back this morning to be cleansed and strengthened. Have mercy on us, and bring us home at last through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Hugh Elmer Brown, Seattle, Wash.

quote: Remember the Sabbath Day.
body: Lord our God, thank you for the rest of the night and the light of a new day, for the guidance of the past week, for work and its rewards, for friendship, and for the comfort of home. We’re glad for this day of rest — let it remind us of Christ, who rose on this very day, and remember that it belongs to him, and to us for his sake. Forgive our past mistakes, and free us from any habit of thought, speech, or action that dishonors you. Keep us patient and kind. Bless the Church and its teachers, and let us end this Sabbath with nothing to regret, carrying courage and self-control into the week ahead. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles Carroll Albertson, D.D., Brooklyn, N.Y.

quote: For thy name’s sake, lead me, and guide me.
body: Lord, hear our prayer this morning — we need you all day, every day, but especially now as the night ends and a new dawn breaks, as though you’d made this day just for us. Take our hand, our heart, our mind into yours, and let our steps follow where you’ve already walked. We lift our voices in praise, trusting that whatever road we take, we’ll have good company — the same presence that once turned grief into joy on the road to Emmaus. We’ll sing, walk humbly, and work helpfully all day; since that’s more than we can manage alone, we ask for your strength. Don’t fail us — and at day’s end, bid us a kind goodnight. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop William A. Quayle, St. Paul, Minn.

quote: The Lord shall guide thee continually.
body: God, we ask for the grace we need for today’s work — our hearts are open, waiting on you. A sensitive conscience, steady loyalty, patience under life’s blows, forbearance with others, tenderness toward the needy — all of these are gifts only you can give. Forgive our sins as we forgive those who wrong us. Widen our vision to include personal holiness, honest business, social responsibility, and mission to the world; make the coming of your kingdom the driving passion of our lives. Above all, give us constant fellowship with you through your Spirit, and fill our days with gratitude for the gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Edgar Y. Mullins, D.D., LL.D., Louisville, Ky.

quote: Offer unto God thanksgiving.
body: Father, we ask your blessing. Free us this morning from doubt and everything that pushes us away from you, and draw us close with whatever encouragement strengthens our faith, hope, and loyalty. We confess our sin and ask daily forgiveness for everything in us that falls short. Give us not just clearer sight but the grace to walk in that light. Strengthen us when our burdens are heavy, and remind each of us that you think of us and turn everything toward our good. Make us more devoted in prayer, more urgent for others’ salvation, more watchful over those around us, and quicker to bear one another’s burdens. Comfort the grieving, and forgive us again, we ask, for all our sins. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. J. W. Somerville, Wichita, Kansas.

quote: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice.
body: Heavenly Father, we come before you with the simple confidence of children, trusting that you’re willing to guide us through this day of opportunity, responsibility, and testing. Bless us as a family, and let the Holy Spirit direct us so that in everything we do, we honor you and represent you well. Make us a blessing to everyone whose lives we touch today. Since every day brings its own particular trials, help us meet them and grow stronger through them, leaving something good behind wherever we go. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. W. H. Bucks, Cleveland, Ohio.

quote: Consider the lilies how they grow.
body: God, you know what we need before we ask, and you know every temptation we’ll face today. Help us trust you completely when despair and doubt come knocking. Don’t let us fall prey to needless worry or lose our peace over things that don’t deserve it. Guide us so that we keep our faces turned toward the light, and let our shadows fall behind us. In your mercy, help us notice our blessings, so we can serve you today with a glad heart and a quiet mind, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Charles E. Woodcock, D.D., LL.D., Louisville, Ky.

quote: Walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us.
body: We thank you, God our Father, for every blessing in our lives — everything we have and everything we do comes from your strength. Help us love you fully and serve you with everything we’ve got. We bring our family before you, wherever each one is and whatever they’re facing; if any are sick, troubled, or tempted, be their healer, their comforting friend, their mighty Savior. Bless our daily work, and if it pleases you, let it prosper — but if hardship serves us better, make us patient through it. Guide us through every uncertainty, and forgive our mistakes and our sins, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by S. S. Waltz, D.D., Louisville, Ky.

quote: In his love and in his pity he redeemed them.
body: Our God, Father of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and our Father through him — thank you for your gracious disposition toward us. In love you’ve redeemed us, and in the fullness of your grace you’ve given us your Spirit, your Word, and everything we need for our souls. We’re grateful for your good providence in the comforts of this life. We ask humbly for faith, hope, and love; for purity; for a clear sense of your leading; and for the trust that banishes anxiety. We pray for happiness in our homes, and ask forgiveness for all the sin we freely confess. Bless your Church, our nation, and all people, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Robert W. Thompson, Pittsburg, Kansas.

quote: Come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord... and ye shall be my sons and daughters.
body: Our Father, help us to be true today, faithful, and kind. Let your presence go with us so no evil catches us off guard. Keep us from stumbling; if temptation comes, give us strength to resist it; if trouble waits, let us meet it bravely, trusting your grace is enough. Don’t let sin gain a foothold over us, whether through its hardening deceit or its flattering comfort. Make us generous in judgment, tender- hearted, gentle, and patient in all our dealings. Plant in us a real hatred for everything that corrupts, and a sincere love for what’s pure and Christlike. For Christ’s sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Malcolm James MacLeod, D.D., New York City.

quote: Blessed is the man that maketh the Lord his trust.
body: Almighty God, our Father, we come to you in this early hour to thank you for the care that kept us through the night, and to prepare for whatever this new day holds. We can’t see what’s ahead, but you can — so we place our hands in yours, trusting you to lead us in a way that honors you and makes our lives more fruitful. Share your richest blessings with our loved ones wherever they are. Reach the needy, the distressed, the sick and dying, and everyone searching for salvation. Forgive our sins, and fill us with peace that lets us walk quietly in your presence, today and at the end of this day’s journey home. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop William M. Weekley, D.D., Parkersburg, W. Va.

quote: He ever liveth to make intercession for them.
body: Gracious God, our Father in heaven, we’re grateful that hour by hour our lives have been enriched by knowing Jesus, who brought the infinite near to our small understanding and drew us close to you through his reconciling love. Remembering our stubbornness and our tendency to sin, we humble ourselves before you and confess our failures — forgive us our trespasses. By your Spirit, let us delight in your ways, and let our daily walk commend the gospel to everyone around us. Hear us also on behalf of loved ones near and far, and let your kingdom come and your will be done, on earth as in heaven. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by James W. Thirtle, D.D., LL.D., London, England.

quote: The righteousness which is of faith.
body: Holy Father, thank you for the sweetness and goodness of your love — you’ve sheltered our home, carried our burdens, and supplied every need. Thank you for Jesus our Savior, for the Bible, and for the Church; we praise you for the gospel and for everyone spreading the good news of salvation. May believers everywhere live together in unity, wrapped in love, until all people know Jesus and learn to live and love as he did. Teach us kindness, tenderness, and forgiveness; give us patience, gentleness, and faith. Fill us with your light and send us out to do good, now and forever, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Robert E. Elmore, Cincinnati, Ohio.

quote: Bless thou the Lord, O my soul.
body: Heavenly Father, we’re your children, and we come bringing our thanks and praise. Your love never fails, and your grace is the strength of our hearts — don’t let us forget it. Help us welcome our everyday duties as if done in your sight, treasure our family bonds, and face our difficulties with courage, redeeming the time we’re given. Help us resist temptation, especially the kind that stains our thoughts, and give us the strength to bear life’s burdens cheerfully. Free us from anxiety about the future, trusting that everything works together for good for those who love you. Shape us into the mind of Christ, ready for any sacrifice for the sake of your kingdom. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John Clifford, D.D., London, England.

quote: I love the Lord because he hath heard my voice.
body: You who light the path for everyone walking alone through shadowed places — teach us to trust you so completely that fear no longer holds us. We confess we’ve often faltered, trading your all-knowing wisdom for our own anxious guesses. Teach us more about the strength of a pure life, and forgive us for doubting your love. Even if we can’t see past the next bend in the road, let us feel the companionship that walks with us into whatever comes. Give us Christ’s peace to calm our restless hearts, and courage for each day’s test of faith. Lead us to rest and renewal, so we can serve you more faithfully in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles Gorman Richards, D.D., Auburn, N.Y.

quote: I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.
body: 122:1 Lord Jesus Christ, who rose from the grave on this day, send your quickening Spirit upon your people, that they may rise to new life. Drive away worldly distractions, and lift our minds to noble and spiritual thoughts. Hear the prayers offered both publicly and privately, for ourselves and for others. Let all who can attend worship do so with reverence and confidence; bless the preaching of your Word and the sacraments, and inspire those who lead with truth, love, and power. Meet the many needs of your people, bind us together in fellowship, and send us out from this day of worship with renewed strength for whatever lies ahead. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Arthur C. A. Hall, Burlington, Vt.

quote: If my people pray, I will forgive their sin.
body: Help us now, Lord, to draw near to you as a family. Turn our hearts toward you, and lift the veil so we can feel your presence. Forgive everything you’ve seen amiss in us, and cleanse our hearts by your Spirit so we can love you fully and honor your name. Having been forgiven so much ourselves, help us forgive others without limit. Keep us from envy, pride, and anything that grieves your Spirit; let us live dead to sin and alive to righteousness through Jesus Christ. Bless those we love, comfort them in every circumstance, and have mercy on everyone, bringing them to know the truth, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. F. B. Meyer, B.A., London, England.

quote: Ask counsel, we pray thee, of God.
body: Heavenly Father, you made us for yourself, and you’re more thoughtful of our welfare than we are ourselves. We feel our weakness; temptation presses in, and we’re too easily drawn off course. Wake in us a sincere longing for you and your house, and help us understand that our souls will never be satisfied until they’re satisfied in you. We feel your call to do our best — don’t let us settle into false security or comfortable sin, and when we’re tempted to think we’ve arrived, remind us how far we still have to grow. When the way feels hard and the easy detour looks tempting, give us your gracious help. Forgive our sins, and let your kingdom and will be done, on earth as in heaven, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Lawrence H. Seager, D.D., Waterville, Ill.

quote: With thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
body: Father in heaven, we praise you for the mercy seat where you welcome us. Help us come with pure hearts and honest motives, and teach us how much we need you — show us how dangerous it is to live without a sense of your presence. Walk with us as Jesus walked with his companions on the road to Emmaus; let us know you as a friend knows a friend. Keep us from willful sin, and calm our rebellious hearts. Help us be patient and understanding with anyone who needs our help; if we’ve wronged someone, give us the grace to make it right, and if we’ve been wronged, help us forgive and let it go. Bless our home and everyone dear to us, in the name of the one who loved us and gave his life to save us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by H. W. Crews, D.D., Woodstock, Ont., Canada.

quote: Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven.
body: Almighty God, we praise your name — you’re infinitely holy, and through Jesus Christ, our elder brother and mediator, you’re our Father too. Draw near to us as we come to your throne of grace. Help us trust you more each day, whether you send darkness and storm or brightness and peace; make us content with your will, only stay close through it all. Bless this home — every one of us, father, mother, children — and make it a place of real security. Guide us in and out, and let your will be done in us as it is in heaven. Fill our lives with your praise, forgive our sins, and give us the joy of your salvation, through Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. H. Dunbar, D.D., Baltimore, Md.

quote: Pray and make supplication.
body: Lord our God, thank you for revealing yourself to us as Father through Jesus Christ your Son, our Savior. Thank you for your loving care through another day — for life, health, and every comfort. Bless us as parents and children; keep us from sinning against you, and help us be faithful in our work, thoughtful toward each other, and kind and helpful to everyone. Watch over us through the night, and bring us safely to another day, so that with each passing day we trust you more and walk more closely in your ways, becoming more like the one who taught us to pray: “Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name...” Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles H. Robinson, D.D., Wheeling, W. Va.

quote: Put on the whole armor of God.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for the rest of the night and the light of this new day, and for food, clothing, and every other blessing you’ve provided out of your goodness. Give us grace for today’s temptations and strength for whatever duty lies ahead. Help us truly represent you, keeping your Word in our hearts so we don’t sin against you or anyone else. Give us the guidance of your good Spirit; protect and defend us from harm, and when our work is done, bring us home safely, in the name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by James M. S. Isenberg, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: That ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will.
body: Father, worthy of all honor and praise, whom we long to worship in spirit and truth — help us come humbly to you in this quiet hour. As your hand watched over us through the night, guiding us into peaceful sleep, now guide our feet into the day’s duties and shield us from harm. Give us your spirit of love and tenderness, your grace to hold us steady through temptation and trial, and your presence to help us in everything we do. Live in this home always, and lead us on to glorify you until, our work here finished, you welcome us into your presence above. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. P. H. Balsbaugh, Columbia, Pa.

quote: Whatsoever ye ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
body: Heavenly Father, we gratefully acknowledge your ongoing kindness in protecting us, sleeping and waking, and providing for our daily needs. Don’t let the regularity of your mercies make us take them for granted — if you ever withheld even one, we’d immediately plead for its return. Help us meditate on your majesty and power, your tender compassion, and your grace to help in our time of need. Above all, thank you for the Son of your love, your greatest gift to us. Help us walk faithfully through the unknown path of another day, and at day’s end, let us look back grateful that we heard your voice and followed. Guide us, comfort us, and forgive us all our sins, for the sake of Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. G. E. Morgan, M.A., London, England.

quote: To all which believe, he is precious.
body: Heavenly Father, source and sustainer of life, from whom we came and to whom we’re going — let our souls be aware of the larger life we’re part of, and help us understand its eternal truths and feel its powerful current carrying us toward your purposes. Thank you for Jesus, and for the way faith in him makes that same divine life real in us. Forgive us for shrinking your life within us down to our own small concerns, for staying aloof from the wider world, and for spending our energy on lesser things. Help us widen and deepen what we experience, stay in sympathy with all humanity, and play a genuine part in bringing the whole family of God to know the fullness of his life. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles Herbert Rust, D.D., Rochester, N.Y.

quote: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid.
body: Lord God, help us pray that today we might come closer to the character of Christ than ever before, and that by every thought and action we might reflect him to everyone we meet. Don’t let us waste a single chance to be living witnesses for him. Carry us safely through whatever dangers and temptations surround us, seen and unseen, to the end of the day and, one day, to the end of this earthly life. Bless those close to us through home and friendship, and reveal yourself with power today, especially to those who don’t yet know you. May the gospel’s note of love ring out more clearly than ever, bringing cheer to the desolate and hope to the despairing. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. W. M. Gross, Cincinnati, Ohio.

quote: Ye have not, because ye ask not.
body: Heavenly Father, we come to you rejoicing — through your Son you’ve brought life and immortality to light, and shown us the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. We confess our sins and ask forgiveness. Bless us today with the sense of your presence, your peace, and your power; use us in your service, and make us living sacrifices — eyes, ears, lips, hands, and hearts all devoted to you. Bless everyone in this family circle: you’ve given us shelter and daily bread, so give us also the bread of heaven and the assurance of an inheritance that never fades. Protect us in danger, deliver us from temptation, and hasten the day when Jesus Christ is acknowledged everywhere as King of kings. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. DeWitt M. Benham, Ph.D., Baltimore, Md.

quote: Before they call, I will answer.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for our home, our work, and our friends. This morning calls us to the joys, labor, and trials of a new day, and we want to begin it rightly, aware of your nearness. Give us strength for our common duties and grace to live happily and helpfully with our family and friends — at school, at home, and in our work, guide us by the purposes of Jesus. If it’s your will, spare us from great temptation, and give us strength for whatever trials you do allow. Comfort and heal those we love who are sick or grieving, and prosper our work so we can use what we gain for the good of others. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Ozora S. Davis, D.D., Ph.D., Chicago, Ill.

quote: Hast thou faith? Have it to thyself before God.
body: Almighty and living God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, look on us, your children, with love and mercy throughout this day. Keep us in faith and reverence; give us grace to resist evil and renounce its works. Guard us from the corruptions of the world, and make us diligent and faithful in our work, patient under trial, and trusting in the midst of worry. We offer you our thoughts, words, and actions today, and ask your blessing on them. Be our healing in sickness and our strength in distress. Bless our friends and neighbors, and comfort their sorrows. Protect your Church everywhere, and guide us by your counsel toward the glory that awaits us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by George McClellan Fiske, D.D., Providence, R.I.

quote: He is faithful that promised.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for watching over us safely into another day of work, delight, and trial. Give us strength to resist evil and hold to what’s good, and let our lives shine so others see your goodness in us. Be with all of us, whether we’re headed to work, to school, or staying to tend the home. Bless every family that remembers you, and let family devotion take root in homes that don’t yet know you. Bless our Church and every church working to advance your kingdom, and send more workers into the harvest. Bless our nation and its leaders with wisdom and courage for justice, at home and abroad, and grant fairness and peace among all the nations of the earth. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Chr. Staebler, Cleveland, Ohio.

quote: He forgave their iniquity.
body: Lord, you’ve proven yourself trustworthy — we ask your blessing as this day begins, so its influence carries us through the toil ahead. Give us the wisdom to do our work the way a well-taught apprentice learns from a master craftsman, and let our minds be shaped by your purposes today. Rule us by your Spirit so that everything about us serves you. Keep us from shameful sin, and from being petty, irritable, or unkind toward others. Be our unseen companion as we earn our daily bread — and help us earn it honestly. Make us wholesome and good- natured, so that others sense, through our quiet goodness, that Christ lives in our house. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by J. Bradley Markward, D.D., Harrisburg, Pa.

quote: I have loved thee with an everlasting love.
body: Loving Father, thank you for watching over us through another night — you never slumber, and your protecting hand has been under and around us the whole time. You’re setting before us a new day full of possibility for good or ill; give us the strength you’ve promised, matched to whatever the day demands. Don’t let us go into today’s duties without your guiding, protecting hand. Give us strength to overcome every temptation, and surround us with your presence as a shield against every danger. Bless everyone we should remember before you, suited exactly to what each of them needs. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by R. J. Miller, D.D., Pittsburgh, Pa.

quote: Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness.
body: Almighty God, our Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us to call you “Father.” In the strength of that name we go out to meet today’s temptations and duties — make us worthy of the name. Give us your patience and tenderness in dealing with others, especially our own family, and compassion for anyone weak or tempted, lending them our strength as you lend yours to us. Clothe us today in the armor of light; give us a hatred of everything impure and a passion for holiness instead. Whatever we do, let it please you, and bring us safely at last to our Father’s house in peace, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Henry Everson Cobb, D.D., New York City.

quote: Wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.
body: In the name of the Lord Jesus we come before you, God, to thank you for your goodness to our family and household, and to ask forgiveness for everywhere we’ve sinned and grieved your Spirit. We pray for grace to walk in a way that pleases you, and for your protection from accident and danger. Above all, walking in your love, may we know the joy of your salvation. And what we ask for ourselves, we ask for everyone dear to us — especially anyone in sickness, sorrow, or trouble, that you’d comfort and sustain them. You gave your only Son so that whoever believes might have eternal life; for everyone who trusts in him, we make this prayer, for Christ’s sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Sir Robert Anderson, K.C.B., LL.D., London, England.

quote: Ask thy Father and he will show thee.
body: Almighty and eternal Lord, we come to you the way you’ve appointed — through the name above every name, and for the sake of the one who bears it. What grace you have for anyone in need, what love and compassion! We praise you for your Son and for all he’s become to those who trust him, and especially for his cross, where we find our hope. Create in us a simple faith in your Word, so we know that nothing you’ve promised will ever fail. Keep increasing our faith, keep us walking with you, and guard us from every attack of the evil one. Help us in our daily work, whatever it is, so we honor and glorify you and bless the people around us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Joseph W. Kemp, New York City.

quote: Sing unto the Lord with thanksgiving.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for opening the door to a new day. Now that we stand on the threshold of this fresh opportunity, we ask for guidance, wisdom, love, and strength. You’ve drawn a curtain over our eyes so we can’t see what the day will bring, but we know that with your help we’ll come through more than conquerors, through the one who loved us. Keep us, God — our boat is so small, and your ocean so vast. Help us set aside every weight that holds us back, and let your fatherly protection cover everyone dear to us. Even bless our enemies, if we have any, and give us goodwill toward everyone. Hasten the day when injustice and unhappiness give way to love, truth, and justice. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Charles C. Selecman, Los Angeles, California.

quote: He hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him.
body: Our Father in heaven, look with favor, in this new morning’s light, on your dependent children gathered here as a family of worshipers in the home you’ve given us. Receive our humble thanks for your perfect care and for the refreshment of restful sleep through the night just past. Now, for yet another day, grant us your watchful care against sickness and danger; your wise counsel for right thoughts and fitting words; your sufficient grace against temptation and for faithfulness in duty; and your forgiving love covering all our sin. Cleanse our hearts of every unworthy motive, and let us walk in charity toward everyone around us, offering some glimpse of your coming kingdom, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Nolan R. Best, New York City.

quote: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
body: God, giver of light and power — thank you for our mountaintop moments, our hours of insight and joy. But insight alone hasn’t made us effective in service; like the disciples at the foot of the mountain, we often find we’re “not able,” and we come to you asking why. We know that faith-filled prayer, whether fellowship with you or intercession for someone else, gets things done — help our unbelief. Bring us so closely into fellowship with you that we’re filled with a power that isn’t our own, truly identified with you, so that today becomes a day of continual joy because your power moves freely in us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by William Horace Day, B.D., D.D., Los Angeles, California.

quote: He forgetteth not the cry of the humble.
body: Dear Lord, our friend and Savior — your children come to your feet and look up into your face, knowing you love us and you’re waiting for us. Be the center of our family life, and let us find our peace and happiness in your presence — our home can only be blessed when we know you’re with us. Help us love each other the way you love us: gently, unselfishly, forgivingly. Calm our fears when we’re troubled, give us victory when we’re tempted, wrap us in your everlasting arms when we’re sick, and seek us out like a shepherd when we wander. May our hearts be glad in your love, and our thoughts pure because you rule them. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Floyd W. Tomkins, B.D., LL.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: God hath attended to the voice of my prayer.
body: God of all grace, Father of mercies, hope of believers, Savior of the penitent soul — hear our prayer. You’ve shown yourself in such lovely, endearing ways that we can set aside our fear and draw near to you with confidence in any trouble. Teach us, Lord, because we don’t know the truth about ourselves; let us see things clearly, so our minds are informed and our hearts made holy at once. Devote our whole lives to your service and glory. Search us, God, and know our hearts; see if there’s any wrong way in us, and lead us in the way everlasting. Accept our thanks for every material and spiritual blessing, and keep us under your care so that whatever we do, we do it for your glory, through Christ our Redeemer and Friend. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by George M. Diffenderfer, D.D., Carlisle, Pa.

quote: This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments.
body: Lord, high and lofty, dwelling in eternity, yet at home also with the humble and contrite in spirit — we come before you asking pardon for our sins through our Savior. Thank you for loving us enough to give your beloved Son so we might live, and we rejoice that no one can snatch us from your hands. May your kingdom come and your will be done, on earth as in heaven. Support everyone laboring for you, whether at home or on the mission field, and comfort everyone sick, bereaved, or troubled, drawing them closer to you through their trials. Give us grace and power to live rightly today, to do our work, and to glorify you — and keep us from anything that would grieve you or bring sorrow to ourselves or anyone else. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by D. T. Reed, Pittsburgh, Pa.

quote: He that hath my commandments and keepeth them, loveth me.
body: Most gracious, all-wise, all-loving God, our Heavenly Father, we rejoice that you’ve called us to be your children. We confess we’re like little children in our weakness and imperfection, but often without their humility, purity, and trust — cleanse us from our sins, and grant us joy and peace in believing, with a love that endures all things. In our homes, our work, our leisure, and all our relationships, make us steadfast for what’s right. Bless us so we become a blessing to others. Remember all people in every condition — the sick, the sorrowful, the poor, the widowed, and the young — and bless the missionaries and teachers spreading your truth around the world, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rufus W. Miller, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Continue in prayer, and watch.
body: Father God, thank you today for life — for the sheer privilege of living. Help us remember that we live in deeds, not years; in thoughts, not merely breaths; that our time is best measured by heartbeats, not the numbers on a clock. Help us act today in a way that shows our gratitude for life. Thank you, too, for the chance to serve — let us not miss any opportunity today to lend a hand, speak a kind word, or show sympathy, and help us truly appreciate the service others give us. Whatever we do today, let it be our very best, and let us press on toward the spiritual life we long for, so that the best we give to the world comes back to us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by D. Walter Morton, A.M., C.P.A., Eugene, Oregon.

quote: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
body: — Romans 8:26 The road is long, our Father, and sometimes very tiring. We crowd and bruise each other as we pass, and often lose sight of the goal in the rush of the journey. Send us out each day with fresh courage, and put a quiet song in our hearts to lighten our steps as we take up our burdens again. Let our conscience be the lightest of all our loads, and don’t let us grow so weighed down by our own troubles that we forget compassion for friend and foe alike. Above all, give us clear vision, so we can see past the doubts and fears of the moment and rest steady in the certainty of your love. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from Louisville, Ky.

quote: O satisfy us early with thy mercy.
body: Dear Lord, let us do our work each day, and if hours of despair overtake us, help us remember the strength that comforted us before. In these times when the world offers so many distractions, let the same power that first turned our lives from darkness into light stay present, refining our hearts like fire. Let your Word be a lamp to our feet and a light to our path. Lift our eyes off the ground; keep us from judging others, so we’re not judged ourselves. Help us understand your Word, and at this point in history, keep us watching eagerly for your return, ready like the wise virgins with lamps trimmed and burning. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. A. Sheldrick, East Northfield, Mass.

quote: The Lord loveth the righteous.
body: God our Father, how precious it is to have your name lingering on our lips, reassuring us that we’re within the circle of your love and care. Let that confidence chase away every fear and anxiety, and keep out every other enemy of our souls today. In moments of temptation, remind us of your promise and your presence; when burdens grow heavy, let us find the strength we need in you. Whatever these hours bring, may your grace be enough, and whatever we do, may we do it for your glory. We leave our prayer where every prayer belongs — in the shadow of the cross. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Cortland Myers, A.B., D.D., Boston, Massachusetts.

quote: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock.
body: Lord, you’re always knocking at the door of our souls, seeking to come in. Help us recognize your knock, and open the door. May our hearts stay open to you always — in sunshine or shadow, joy or sorrow. Whether you come in springtime birdsong or winter’s cold, may we welcome you gladly. Show us that we need you more than anything you could give us, and that you, yourself, are worth more than all your gifts. So when you knock, Lord, may we open to you and receive you as a lasting guest. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by H. H. Beattys, D.D., New Rochelle, New York.

quote: The Lord hath dealt bountifully with thee.
body: God, in whose hand is our very breath — you’ve held all our yesterdays and already know what our tomorrows hold. Thank you for today. We try to keep pace with your sun, and so we add this extra day to our year — though we could never really keep up with the sheer scale of your gifts, since you do far more for us than we could ever ask or imagine. When we give ourselves to you, you give back overflowing measure — surprises, growth, experiences beyond what eye has seen or ear has heard, an inexhaustible Christ, and endless forgiveness. Fill our hearts with deeper love, so we grow ever more grateful, setting aside our complaints and bitterness for the fresh joy that belongs to this new life you’ve called us into. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. C. Bitting, D.D., St. Louis, Missouri.

quote: Let them that love thy name be joyful in thee.
body: Gracious Father, we lift our hearts to you, the only source of our strength. Help us trust you so fully that we trust you even in the dark. Your mercies are new every morning and renewed every night — help us praise you for your goodness and rest in your love. You know what we need before we ask; grant us all you see we need, and save us from suffering, doubt, and sin. Free us from anxiety, so our minds are unburdened enough to comfort and understand others. Make us useful wherever you’ve placed us, and forgive our sins through Jesus Christ; shape us more and more into his likeness, and bring us at last to dwell forever in your presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Benjamin B. Warfield, D.D., LL.D., Princeton, N.J.

quote: Make the voice of his praise to be heard.
body: Father, thank you for the day ahead — its light woke us with gladness, and its evening shadows will call us to rest, a picture of the life you’ve given us: joy and sorrow, toil and hope, memory and promise woven together. Help us be grateful and worthy of this gift. Above all, we’re thankful for this household — through it we understand you better, the way parenthood draws us near to you and childhood draws our children near to us. Bless our children and everyone we love, and make each of us worthy of trust, human and divine. We’re sorry for every harsh word and unkind act — as we forgive one another, forgive us too, Father, for every failure against you. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by N. McGee Waters, D.D., Brooklyn, New York.

quote: He will be our guide even unto death.
body: Almighty and merciful Father, we begin the day aware of our own helplessness and your supreme power. As you gave us life, sustain it, and prepare us for greater service. Thank you for your care through the night — day and night are alike to you. Just as you’ve watched over our rest, we trust you’re planning our whole path; prepare us for whatever you’re preparing for us. If we fail to live up to your plan, correct us gently and restore us. If disappointment or sorrow comes, make us strong to bear it, enriched by your sustaining grace. Keep us faithful in every duty, and bind us as a family with a sacred love, worthy of your continuing care. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by James E. Freeman, D.D., Minneapolis, Minn.

quote: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
body: 2 Corinthians 5:1 Father in heaven, thank you for the mercies of the past day and night — for food and clothing, sleep and shelter, the companionship of others, and daily chances to be useful. As we receive these gifts, help us also recognize the responsibilities they carry, so our love for you and for others keeps growing stronger through daily practice. Give us grace to face the future with a steady heart. We deeply believe in life beyond this one — that you haven’t given the human mind such remarkable capacity for discovery and progress only for it to vanish into nothing at death. We believe you’ve given each of us a soul able to dwell with you forever; help us live now in a way that prepares us for that eternal home, and help us, by word and example, lead others to trust Jesus Christ and share in that same hope. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: God forbid that I should sin in ceasing to pray.
body: Father in heaven, we turn to you this morning with grateful hearts for your care through the night. Thank you for home, food, and clothing, for the work you’ve called us to, for health enough to serve you, for friends to love, and above all for your revelation of yourself through Jesus Christ our Lord. Bless our home today; guard each of us against temptation, and keep us from selfishly hoarding any blessing you’ve given us. Fill our lives with the joy and peace that comes from obeying you. Cleanse and strengthen your Church for the work it’s called to, and empower everyone preaching your Word near and far. Grant everyone we love your richest blessing today, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. B. Anderson, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labor of love.
body: Thessalonians 1:2–5 Eternal God, our Father — before we go out to meet the world’s trials and temptations, we come to you for strength to steady our spirits. Give us your own armor: truth in our thoughts and motives, a sense of duty in our work and relationships, and courage to face difficulty because we know we’re honest and that you’re with us. Let our daily tasks, ordinary or important, be lifted up by the knowledge that we’re doing your will. Give us patience with others’ shortcomings and wisdom in shaping our own character. Don’t let anything today mar the structure of our lives — keep us unstained by the world, and watch over us while we’re apart from one another. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. W. B. Anderson, Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.
body: Father in heaven, we bless you for being near, not far off. Thank you for your protecting care and sustaining grace; we’re grateful for material comfort and the joy of friendship, and we see your hand in every good thing. Forgive our past sins through God’s mercy, and make us pure, strong, and honest today. Bless us and everyone dear to us, and all humanity — may your kingdom come, and righteousness and peace govern every human relationship. Let us go to our work today in reverence and a joyful sense of your presence, and when evening comes, let us rest knowing that our Keeper never sleeps. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. A. S. Tuttle, M.A., Medicine Hat, Alta., Canada.

quote: Ask of God, and he will give it thee.
body: Father, thank you for our home, its shelter and its loving fellowship — whatever else it may lack, make it rich in the full presence of your Holy Spirit. Forgive and forget the sins of our lives, for our Savior’s sake, and cleanse us in his precious blood. Send each of us out filled with his spirit of unselfish service. Strengthen us for every proper task, teach us kindness toward others in Christ’s name, and make us channels of your mercy, leading us into the path where we can best glorify you and serve our fellow men. Make our home life more and more Christlike, and hasten, through our service, the coming of your worldwide kingdom, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Prof. William J. Martin, Davidson, N.C.

quote: The Lord is good to the soul that seeketh him.
body: Infinite Father, you are our life and light, our hope and redemption. We’ve tried the world and found it empty; we come back to you, eager to fill our souls with lasting truth and mercy. We come with a song in our hearts, for your gifts to us are beyond counting. Thank you for the stimulating challenges of the present, with its chances to grow and serve, and for the uncertain days ahead, whatever they hold. Thank you for the quiet heroism of home and the unnoticed labor of caring for the sick. Even though we so often frustrate your plans and wander from Jesus’ way, we come to you this morning to be cleansed and strengthened. Have compassion on us, and bring us all home at last through the riches of grace in Christ Jesus. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Hugh Elmer Brown, Seattle, Washington.

quote: We are more than conquerors through him that loved us.
body: Heavenly Father, strength of everyone who trusts you, be with us each day to steady our hands and guide our hearts, so we give our best in your service. You know our weakness, how much we care what others think — give us your strength so we’re never afraid to do your will. Every day brings temptation, sorrow, and success; help us meet each one with clear faith and honest trust in your goodness. As we go about our work, in office or school or home, give us pure thoughts and clean speech. Help us make someone happier each day by word or deed, so that as evening falls we can rest knowing we’ve served the world well. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. E. H. Bonsall, Jr., Morton, Pa.

quote: He knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
body: Lord, we come to you in the name of Jesus, who is the way, the truth, and the life. You’re a great God, deserving of reverence and holy awe, but you’re also our Father, our creator and redeemer, and we come with a child’s love and confidence. Thank you for the friend and advocate we have in heaven — our Savior, tempted in every way as we are yet without sin, who understands our weaknesses. We adore you, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Every good gift comes from you; all our hope rests in you. Don’t cast us from your presence — look on us with compassion, and blot out our sins. Teach us your will, and lead us on a clear path, growing in grace as we grow in years. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles P. Wiles, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: We are bound to thank God always.
body: Father, thank you that your mercies are still upon us and your love still surrounds us. We bless you for the joy of simply existing, and for every good and beautiful thing you’ve placed in our lives — beauty is set all around us, and you reach for us through every sense we have. We know your mercy, because you’ve never once treated us as our sins deserved. As another day ends, we come for your blessing, entrusting ourselves to the love that has never failed us. Look on us with tender compassion, and take away our wrongs; let your everlasting arms hold us up. Teach us to do your will, and lead us in the way everlasting. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by David F. McGill, D.D., Ben Avon, Pa.

quote: God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.
body: Gracious God and Father, we praise you for constant access to you through Jesus Christ, and bless you for your daily gifts to spirit, soul, and body. Thank you for your unchanging love and grace, from which we can draw at every moment according to our need. Give us a deepening sense of how precious Christ is as our Redeemer, and a growing confidence in the Spirit’s constant supply for daily living. Teach us, by that Spirit, to depend continually on your grace, receiving it by simple faith and making full use of what you provide. Let your love show in our daily conduct, driving us to live for your praise and to help others just as you’re helping us. Bless our relatives and friends with every needed grace, and deepen our sense of your love so we’re moved to share the gospel far and wide. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Ask, and it shall be given you.
body: Heavenly Father, accept our thanks for the rest and renewal you’ve given our bodies and minds through the gift of sleep. Help us stay so attentive to the quiet voice of your Spirit that whatever we do today, it’s done for your glory. We want your kingdom to come and your will to be done in our hearts, our home, our city, our country, and the whole earth — and to that end, we offer you our bodies, minds, and lives, to use as you see best. Connect us and everything we have to your work in the world, and teach us through your Word to trust you daily, staying peaceful and joyful whether we face hardship or prosperity. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by William B. Stubbs, Savannah, Georgia.

quote: I will extol thee, my God, O King; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.
body: Psalm 145:1–4 We thank you, Father in heaven, for life and health and home. You’ve brought us this new day with its new blessings and duties; as we head into our tasks and pleasures, let our hearts stay full of love for you and everyone around us. We place our hands in yours, trusting you to lead us on a right and safe path. We’re glad to know you’re with us, and we won’t do anything that would drive you away. Teach us to walk in Jesus’ footsteps, who went about doing good. Bless every member of our family, our friends, and even our enemies, if we have any, and let our eyes, ears, and hearts turn toward what’s true, clean, and good. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by J. C. Armstrong, D.D., Kansas City, Missouri.

quote: The unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice.
body: Father, thank you for binding this family together by the sacred tie of common blood — created and sustained, we know, through so much sacrificial love. We bless you for a mother’s labor and tenderness, and a father’s faithful work. Knit us together through shared joys and sorrows, so that even when we’re far apart, nothing estranges our hearts. When the youngest of us grows old, may the memories of this home stay sweet, and may our children’s children carry forward the strength and faith of those who came before them. Deal graciously with our loved ones; give us our daily bread and strength for our work, and we commit each life and future to you through Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice.
body: Lord, our Lord, how excellent is your name in all the earth. You’re our God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we, your children by faith, have forgiveness of sins. As our ancestors trusted you, we too, their children, want to reverently worship and adore you. We give humble thanks for your great love shown in Christ, and for your rich, unfailing provision for us and for all people. For Jesus’ sake, accept our thanks, continue your favor toward us, and grant pardon and eternal life. Give us your Holy Spirit as our guide today, into truth — let the Spirit comfort us in sorrow, strengthen us in weakness, lift us when we fall, and help us do your will gladly. Bless our nation and the whole world with heavenly peace, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John Grant Newman, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Thy face, Lord, will I seek.
body: Heavenly Father, before we take up the work of this new day, we bow before you together in prayer, asking to be truly aware of your presence as we begin. Help us recognize, in everything we do today, that the quiet voice calling us toward what’s best is your voice; that the tug at our hearts is your hand; and that the light guiding our path is your love. May we walk with you today as your Spirit leads, following the example of Jesus Christ, our righteous Savior. We offer you the love and gratitude of our hearts for every blessing we enjoy. Take each of us into your loving care as we go out today, and gather us home at last, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Frank G. Smith, Kansas City, Missouri.

quote: Therefore shall the people praise thee.
body: Almighty God, Heavenly Father, light and life of all people, we give humble and hearty thanks for every blessing of your Providence, and we entrust ourselves and everyone dear to us — family, friends, neighbors — to your divine care. Give us grace to live so that we’re not afraid to die; save us from every danger of soul and body, and grant us strength for our work, enough for our needs, and good judgment in everything. We pray for our country, that it might be exalted in righteousness, that its leaders would be wise and just, and its citizens faithful and law-abiding — a land of liberty, peace, and true religion. Finally, protect and encourage everyone proclaiming the gospel at home and abroad, and let your kingdom be established over all the earth, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Thomas F. Gailor, D.D., Memphis, Tennessee.

quote: Thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin.
body: Lord Jesus, our Redeemer, stay present with us today. As the all-seeing Savior, you know every one of our ways — nothing is hidden from you. You know how sin threatens us daily, how temptation surrounds us on every side, how doubt fills our hearts with distrust, and how life’s worries make us anxious about tomorrow and forgetful of your promises. In your mercy, help us look up to you in faith. Give us strength against today’s sins and temptations, help us set our worries aside, and trust you with a child’s simple faith. Above all, forgive us where we’ve failed before, and let us find in you the Savior whose blood has redeemed us from sin and death. Fill us, your forgiven children, with love for you and for others. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Alfred Doerffler, St. Louis, Missouri.

quote: The Lord preserveth the faithful.
body: Almighty and most merciful God, we humble ourselves before you, adoring your power as much as your love, your generosity as much as your compassion. Lord, give us what you know we need better than we know how to ask. Direct all our affairs graciously today; bless our household duties and our home life, and go with everyone heading out to the work of the world, prospering their labor and their plans. Find some meaningful way for each of us to help someone today, and let us find it too. Surround our loved ones with the same gracious care, wherever they are and whatever they face. Lift our eyes beyond our own small circle of concern to the great work and kingdom of God, of which we’re a part. Forgive our many sins, and guide us today so we meet temptation led by the Spirit, finding a way through it and moving safely forward in faith, hope, and loving service. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Melvin Grove Kyle, D.D.

quote: The Lord is the strength of my life.
body: Gracious Father in heaven, we accept with grateful hearts this wonderful privilege of coming into your presence through prayer. A new day stretches ahead, and we don’t know what it holds before it ends — how badly we need a strength beyond our own. We find ourselves unequal to the day’s tasks; our vision is narrow, our judgment faulty, our wisdom incomplete, and we’re becoming more aware of our shortcomings — how much more clearly you must see them. Forgive us and help us; teach us that we’re strongest when, in weakness, we throw ourselves entirely on you, and that losing ourselves is how we gain real influence. Help us be good witnesses for Jesus Christ today, so our lives ring true and it’s easier for others to do right simply because we’re in the world. Make us strong in temptation, and give us grace for whatever trial comes, through Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. William S. Abernethy, D.D.

quote: They shall prosper that love thee.
body: Heavenly Father, we bow humbly before you, acknowledging your goodness and confessing you as our God. Thank you for your countless mercies and continued love and care toward us, though we’re unworthy of any of it. We confess our sins, and ask that for Christ’s sake you’d forgive us and help us live so that we carry his spirit everywhere we go. Give us purity of heart, so that we’re always able to see you. Help us notice our opportunities each day to serve others and bring glory to your name. Lead us day by day, so we follow you obediently and lovingly, expressing Christ’s love so clearly that others are drawn to accept him as Savior and Lord. Be gracious to everyone in sadness or difficulty, helping them trust you and feel your presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by I. G. Bowles, B.A., B.D., North Bay, Ont., Canada.

quote: I will give thanks unto thee forever.
body: Eternal Father, help us think wise thoughts, speak kind words, and do good deeds through every hour of this new day. Help us see things as they are, and also as they ought to be; we want a hand in making the world better, and since the nearest duties matter most, let us begin at home — dedicating our energy to being cheerful and helpful to the people we love. Let us lift the burdens of the weary and bring joy to the sorrowful under our own roof, then share that same strength with others, near and far. A single day holds so much possibility for good — help us make the most of it. Give us a fresh sense of your love and the worth of life, so that when our time comes, we can say we lived and gave gladly. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles Frederic Goss, D.D., Cincinnati, Ohio.

quote: The prayer of faith shall save.
body: Lord, increase our faith. By it may we move mountains of difficulty out of our path, and let it be our shield against the arrows of temptation. May it steady and encourage us as we shape our plans and take up our duties in line with your will. May it free us from anxious worry about ourselves and the loved ones we entrust to your care, and incline us toward forgiveness, patience, and sympathy. May it save us from being too swayed by praise or too crushed by blame, and give fresh energy to our daily work. May it teach us humility in prosperity and keep us from bitterness in sorrow, strengthening our hold on what truly lasts. May it assure us, each day of our journey, that you’re near, walking and talking with us as with a friend. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.
body: Father, we thank you for the morning light and for all your goodness. We confess our faults, failures, and sins, and ask your pardon. Give us sound judgment to see what you want from us, a ready will to do our duty fully, and the help of your Spirit to live according to your will today. Look with compassion on everyone in need or trouble, and come to their aid. Strengthen the weak, help the tempted, lift the fallen, comfort the doubting, give patience to the suffering, and courage to the discouraged. Bless our country, and let righteousness and peace prevail among all nations. Bless your Church everywhere, especially those who’ve gone out to preach the gospel in distant lands, and care for everyone dear to us, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Chauncey B. Brewster, D.D., Hartford, Conn.

quote: I was brought low, and he helped me.
body: We thank you, God, that we can call you Father, for no parent loves as deeply as you. We admit with sorrow that we’ve grieved you again and again, since even when we mean to do good, evil is close at hand. But praise God, when we honestly confess our sins, you’re faithful to forgive. Thank you for the daily blessings of life, seen and unseen, and for caring for us even when we’re not thinking of you. Write over our door, “Peace be to this household,” and help us create that same atmosphere within it. Keep us from temptation, make us glad and faithful Christians, and help everything we do, think, and say become a blessing to others. When sorrow comes, may we still praise you and trust you, and when our work is finished, take us to yourself, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by L. M. Zimmerman, D.D., Baltimore, Md.

quote: Let those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee.
body: Father in heaven, we come with deepest gratitude and love — you’ve been a kind Father and a faithful friend. Thank you for daily provision, for guidance in business and at home, for the ordinary mercies that come so regularly we forget to be grateful for them. Most of all, thank you that you love us, that your compassion never runs out, and that your goodness surrounds our incompleteness every day. In your mercy, forgive us — we’re weak, and we sin so easily that we must daily lean on your strength and renew our prayer for pardon. Make us strong against temptation, and help us stay true to what’s pure and Christlike all day. Heal our sick friends, comfort the sorrowful, and give courage and strength to anyone carrying a heavy burden today. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions.
body: Sheltered as we are in the peace of our own home, we pray today for the homeless and the lonely — for wayward souls who’ve wandered far and restless, that their hearts would turn back toward home; for orphaned children who miss a mother’s comfort, that they’d find tenderness elsewhere; for workers separated from their families in distant cities, that they’d overcome the temptations around them; for the selfish and cruel who’ve wrecked their own happiness and others’, that their hearts would be changed. For everyone to whom home is only a memory, a longing, or a regret, we ask, God of infinite compassion, that your love would reach them with a message of new life. Since it’s your will that we carry such messages, prepare us for this work with wider sympathy and readier kindness. In Christ’s name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. A. J. Bonsall, Litt.D., Pittsburgh, Pa.

quote: He forgetteth not the cry of the humble.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for watching over us as we slept, and for bringing us in health and strength to see this new day’s light. But we need you more in daylight than at midnight — open our eyes to today’s opportunities. Like a servant coming to his master each morning for instructions, we come to you seeking guidance. Strengthen our bodies, clear our minds, and warm our hearts, so we live today according to your will and do nothing that displeases you. Bless our home life, so that by example we lead our children rightly, and help us make our households so much like heaven that growing up in your care feels natural to them. Go with us into our wider relationships, so we help rather than hinder, and bless everyone crying out to you for help. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Forney Hutchinson, D.D., Little Rock, Arkansas.

quote: Deliver me, for I do not forget thy law.
body: Heavenly Father, with gratitude and confidence we bow together this morning after the rest of the night. We face the day and its untested challenges with courage and hope, holding to your promise never to fail or forsake us. We place ourselves humbly in your care — forgive us, protect us, guide us, use us, and keep us mindful of you all day. Reveal yourself to everyone dear to us, and lead them into your peace; deliver anyone in temptation, and sustain and comfort anyone in sorrow, supplying every need according to your riches in Christ Jesus. Give our leaders wisdom to govern rightly, unite our people in love and justice, and let those who have help those who don’t, so poverty and oppression fade. Spread the knowledge of your salvation everywhere, and hasten the coming of Christ’s day, in whose name we ask all this. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. George Wells Ely, Columbia, Pa.

quote: Come unto me, and I will give you rest.
body: God, our Father and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Word tells us your Spirit helps us in our weakness, interceding for us according to your will. We yield ourselves to you so your Spirit can work that grace in us now — cleansing our hearts, lifting them in worship, comforting us in trial, strengthening us against temptation, guiding us in your will, and enlightening us in confusion. Pour your love into our hearts, and keep us loving, hopeful, patient, kind, and honest, blessing everyone we meet and glorifying your name, through Jesus Christ our Savior, who loves us and freed us from our sins by his own blood. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by James M. Gray, D.D., Chicago, Illinois.

quote: Thy prayers and thine alms are come up before God.
body: Father in heaven, thank you for this moment of looking to you as the day begins, so we don’t forget its purpose. Thank you for placing us in a world that needs what we have to give, giving meaning to our brief lives. Teach us today to do what pleases you, so that through every difficulty and disappointment we know the peace that passes understanding and stay cheerful. Thank you for the forgiving love we know in you; help us reflect it today, seeing the best in others so we’re kind all day long. Save us from blind selfishness and prideful self- reliance, and let our light shine so that people glorify you for having seen it. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: We trust in the living God, the Saviour of all men.
body: Giver of Life and Love, Author of all our joys — we bless you for your Word, your holy day, the church, and the wondrous sacrifice of our Lord’s redemption. We rejoice in the privilege of prayer, its fellowship with the Divine, and the assurance that you hear and answer. Thank you for the promised Spirit, who strengthens our weak hearts, assures us we’re your children, and helps us overcome every temptation. Help us stand firm in faith and share it with others, doing good and advancing your kingdom across the earth. Bless our home; let it be a place of worship, guarded by your care, so that peace attends every step of our lives until we depart in faith and hope of life everlasting. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Junius B. Remensnyder, D.D., LL.D.

quote: Whoso offereth praise, glorifieth me.
body: Infinite Life, from whom we come and in whom we live and move — Father of our spirits, closer to us than our own breath — we begin this new day with deep gratitude and reverence. Make us glad simply to be alive in a world so full of wonder and beauty. Be our great companion today; let us see you in everyone we meet and find you in every experience. Help us give our very best of mind and heart to today’s tasks, our thoughts so full of goodness and our hands so busy with kindness that there’s no room left for anything unworthy. Let us find happiness not by chasing it, but by bringing it to others, especially those closest to us — living this day fully, in the spirit of Christ, the Master of life. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: We love him, because he first loved us.
body: Gracious God, our Father, thank you for the restful curtain of night. You made everything in this world for our comfort and contentment — walking with you turns any place into a garden, and in your presence is fullness of joy. We bless you for little children — their laughter, trust, and purity — and ask for lessons from their simple happiness. Bless every child touched by our influence; guard us from setting a bad example, and help us teach through the example of our own lives rather than harsh words. Fill our hearts with overflowing love that shapes and softens the young ones around us, replacing arbitrary commands and harsh penalties with patient tenderness, until we’re shaped into the likeness of our Elder Brother, Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The faithful God which keepeth covenant.
body: Heavenly Father, whose life is within us and whose love surrounds us, make that life real in us today as we move through our tasks gladly, without haste or confusion, able to meet every honest demand and find beauty everywhere. Let us move through the hours aware of your presence, breathing an atmosphere of love, seeking to bless others through love rather than anxious effort. Knowing we’re laborers together with you, help us rise above discouragement into the assurance of faith that overcomes the world. And now, let us enter the quiet of your presence, so that hidden with you, our souls are filled with the sense of your care, and our strength renewed. Lay your hand of love on each of us now. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The love of Christ constraineth us.
body: Lord, search our hearts and make them clean. Renew a right spirit within us continually. Make us willing to do your will, and teach us how to pray and how to work. Help us go wherever you send us; give us courage to speak for you and loving patience as we try to help others. Bless every member of our church and Sunday school, and help us soon lead someone to you — show us who we might help, and make us eager to reach them. Fill our hearts with deeper, truer love for you. Forgive our sins, and make us better Christians every day, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Ernest Bourner Allen, D.D., Toledo, Ohio.

quote: His going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain.
body: Hosea 6:3 God, Father, Savior, and Revealer — bless everyone who seeks deeper truth in the midst of what they already know. As they question inherited assumptions, deepen their loyalty to what’s truly eternal. Let intellectual freedom leave their trust in you undamaged, and as the climb toward truth opens wider views of your thought, lead them in the humble, sacrificial path of service. Let them share the joy of their own growth without undermining anyone else’s faith. Don’t let pride of learning cool the warmth of their prayer, and don’t let opposition or misunderstanding breed bitterness in them. As your grace draws them into deeper sympathy with Christ, let them offer the world fresh assurance of his kingdom’s triumph rather than the anguish of their own doubt — and amid every disagreement, may they find the peace that passes understanding in Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: God is faithful, by whom ye were called.
body: Our Father in heaven, you’ve graciously answered our prayer for safety through the darkness of another night. For this mercy we thank you, lifting our refreshed hearts in gratitude and asking your guidance as we begin a new and unknown day.
