Let your Spirit dwell richly in us, making your Father’s love, power, and knowledge real to us — help us grasp what it means that even the hairs of our head are numbered, and remember the deep care of the Good Shepherd who feeds his flock. Let your kingdom come and your will be done in and through us every moment today. Bring your Word to mind in ways that give us vision, inspiration, and faithfulness, so that we’re useful — useful to you by being genuinely helpful to those around us who need to know a Savior’s love. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us.
body: 5:1–2 Father, since you care so deeply about everything we do, help us treat all our work today as done in your sight. Make us faithful and give us the will to do our best in everything, ashamed to shirk any task set before us — at home, at work, or at school — and guided by you as we face it. In work and play alike, help us be fair, honest, and considerate of others, caring more about playing well than winning. Keep us thoughtful and friendly toward others, and guard us against sharp words, unworthy thoughts, and selfish acts. Bind us closer to our loved ones and our friends today, and to you, the friend who sticks closer than a brother, so that by day’s end we’re wiser, stronger, and better able to serve you tomorrow. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Charles W. — (name incomplete in source).

quote: For the Father himself loveth you.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for the peace, rest, and comfort of the night we’ve come through — we have every reason to be grateful for your growing care. You’re always thinking of us, and we sleep safely under your protecting presence. Now we step into the light of another day; let it be a clean, glad, undefiled day, free of dark or impure thoughts, with the grace to set aside everything sinful or selfish. Help us overcome every kind of temptation, and if weakness, weariness, or doubt come, give us your gracious help. In business, at home, and with our friends, make us thoughtful, tender, and generous, carrying the spirit of our Master, who went about doing good. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive.
body: Father in heaven, we come before you in the name of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord and Savior — for his sake, hear our prayer. We offer thanks for your loving kindness and tender mercy, which have never failed us, and we humbly ask forgiveness for our sins, confessing that we’ve often fallen short of your will. But forgiveness is found in you, and that’s why you’re revered. Free us from the power of evil; don’t let any sin rule over us, and shield us from harm in body and spirit. Direct our future, shape our plans, and don’t let us live selfish or wasted lives — let us do good as we’re able and serve our generation according to your will. We entrust to your care everyone we love who’s absent from us, and we pray for your kingdom to come and your Spirit to be poured out on every church. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Mine eyes shall be upon the faithful of the land.
body: Almighty God, our Heavenly Father, in whom we live and move and exist, we come to you, unworthy as we are, with humble hearts to offer prayer and thanks. Forgive the sins we’ve committed in thought, word, and deed, and give us a genuine sorrow that leads to real change. Bless us and our relatives, friends, and neighbors, providing what we need in body and soul. Let your Spirit guide your church and all who serve in it, so your kingdom comes and everyone does their part faithfully. Have mercy on the sick, the dying, and all who struggle with sin. Into your hands we commit our bodies, souls, and spirits — grant us restful sleep, so we can meet tomorrow’s duties with strength of mind and body, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The just shall live by his faith.
body: Gracious and merciful Father, we come to you in the hallowed name of the one who loved us and gave himself for us. Thank you for guarding our home and keeping us safe through the night, and for the promises of your Word, fulfilled for everyone who trusts and obeys you. Thank you for the blessings, opportunities, and chances to serve that have come with this morning. Help us be faithful to your Word in every duty, kind in word and deed, and let your presence turn obedience into our joy in every task or trial. Help us follow our Lord’s example in everything, showing kindness to the poor and needy, and bringing comfort and healing to the sick, the tired, and the lonely everywhere. Remember our pastor and all who preach the gospel at home and abroad, and hasten the coming of Christ’s kingdom. To your name, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, be all the praise. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Thou answeredst them, O Lord our God.
body: Heavenly Father, we bow before you this morning, thankful for the mercy and love that has brought us again into your holy presence. We have sinned — will you forgive us? Thank you for the food you’ve given us; feed our souls too with the bread that comes down from heaven. We bless you for our home and our loved ones, and ask that as you’re present with us here, you’d also stay close to family bound to us by kinship but separated by distance. Thank you for our friends and neighbors, and bless them; thank you for the church, and give it spiritual power for its work in this community and across the land. Supply your grace to the missionaries you’ve sent into the world’s dark places, so that Christ becomes known everywhere and your kingdom comes swiftly. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: So will we sing and praise thy power.
body: Divine Father, who in holy love created and sustains us as your children, we ask your gracious blessing at the threshold of this day — bless us in our going out and our coming in. Fill our hearts with love and our minds with worthy purposes; in our work, help us see the dignity of labor, the reach of sympathy, and the lasting power of integrity, doing good to everyone as we’re able. Move us to relieve suffering, fill us with compassion for the needy, and give us courage to face adversity and resist evil. Strengthen the work of our hands and hearts, and help us overcome temptation. Bring us home from our labor in peace, wrapped in a calm the world can’t provide, and teach us to live greatly and love greatly, so that at life’s evening there’s still light. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised.
body: We rejoice, gracious Lord, that you’re willing to hear your children call on you — no earthly ruler is as open to his people as you are to us. From any place, at any time, with any need, you invite us to open our hearts to you, and you never send us away without an answer. Made bold by your promise and by our own experience of your blessing, we come to you again. We praise you for mercies too great to count, and ask you to forgive our sins — whether wrongdoing, bad temper, or neglected duty — since you delight to pardon. Forgive it all, and seal our hearts with the assurance of peace and acceptance. Shape us more into your likeness, stand with us in temptation, and bring us at last to dwell with you forever. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Jesse L. Hurlbut, D.D., Newark, New Jersey.

quote: He will love thee, and bless thee.
body: Heavenly Father, you’ve been good to us, and we come with love and gratitude to thank you for sound minds, healthy bodies, and every chance to grow and serve. Help us show our gratitude through obedient lives, laboring with joy and trust to make this world brighter and better for everyone — for children to grow up in, and for every father and mother to raise them with a sense of sacred privilege and responsibility. Be merciful to the many families who suffer because of alcohol’s curse; destroy what threatens to destroy those Christ died for. Keep every child untouched by sin, and remember with tenderness the elderly, the lonely, the sick, the tempted, and the discouraged, and everyone suffering because of others’ wrongs. Let joy, peace, harmony, and holiness alone reign in our hearts. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.
body: Father in heaven, thank you for this day and all its opportunities — help us show our gratitude by how we use it. Let Christ so live in our hearts that we’re kept from sin, and rule and bless our home today. Bless our friends and neighbors; let us live before them in a way that honors your name. Bless the poor, the sick, and the suffering, and let their need call us to serve. Bless our church, and give us zeal to win others to Christ. We pray for our town, state, and country, that righteousness would prevail, and for the whole world, that the gospel would spread quickly, wars would cease, and sin and greed would lose their grip — and to that end, may we give as generously as you’ve blessed us. Let your peace fill our hearts today. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: He hath set his love upon me.
body: God of our ancestors, our Father in heaven — you’re good to everyone, and your tender mercy touches all your works. Thank you for night and day, for rest and sleep, for life, light, and love. We confess we sin against you even as we lie down and rise up, but we take shelter in your fatherhood, trusting that for Christ’s sake you forgive us. We entrust ourselves to your faithful care for this day — give your angels charge over us, guide us with your eye, and keep us safe in body and soul, body and spirit, going out and coming in. Help us live together in peace and love, with rule over our own tempers, ready to hear and do your will. Bless our friends and neighbors, and everyone we love, especially anyone sick or troubled — comfort and relieve them quickly. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after.
body: We need you, loving God — without you we’re lonely, discontented, helpless, and defeated. How can we know ourselves rightly unless you teach us? How can we love goodness and find real joy unless your Spirit lives in us? How can we carry our burdens, resist temptation, serve unselfishly, or grow into the character of Christ, unless you take hold of us? We’re grateful that you never withhold yourself from an eager, hungry, willing heart, and that you’re ready to give yourself to us. Teach us to open ourselves to you. Help us obey your will joyfully and work alongside your plans. Correct us when we wander, discipline us when we’re stubborn, encourage us when we’re discouraged, and strengthen us when we’re confused. Shape us through every experience of our lives. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: My lips shall utter praise.
body: Heavenly Father, help us be thankful for our home and all its blessings and privileges. Give each of us eyes to see, and the grace and strength for the duties that are ours. Help us love our home and build it up, and let every home within reach of our influence be blessed because of us. Give us compassion and a helping hand for everyone whose needs call on us, and save us from harm, that we may serve you in purity and strength. Bless our church and everyone who ministers in it, and your servants around the world. Let our faith be genuine and appealing to others, our love voiced through our efforts, gifts, and prayers on behalf of a needy world. Help us stay ready for whatever your providence holds, always saying, in word, thought, and deed, “Thy kingdom come, thy will be done.” Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. M. P. Hunt, Fayetteville, Ark.

quote: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
body: Father, we don’t know what the day will bring, but our help is in you. Thank you for your promised watchfulness, and we ask for faith enough to go forward trusting the one who never slumbers nor sleeps. Keep us true to our calling as followers of Jesus Christ; as we make our living day by day, don’t let us fail to make a life. Help us learn from him who mixed heaven’s glory with earth’s ordinary work — our tasks grow heavy mostly when we forget you. Let us hunger for righteousness enough to trust fully in your protection, so that when other voices tempt us with easy shortcuts, we find our refuge in you instead. Free our hearts from fret and worry today, and let your peace, beyond understanding, be ours. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Edwin H. Bonsall, Jr., Morton, Pa.

quote: Rest in the Lord, and wait patiently for him.
body: Holy Father, thank you for the gift of life, of reason, of love. We are small, but you are great — and yet it’s a great thing to matter so little and still be loved by you. With a single measure you span the heavens you made, yet you take your whole strength to carry a single lost lamb. We’re confident of your love; give us faith, forgiveness, and the power of your Spirit, so our confidence rests firmly in you. Give us today a sound mind in a sound body, wisdom, self-control, and the right attitude toward you, toward others, and toward everything good. Help us understand that the truly great deed is the deed of service — let us do good quietly, not to be seen, and find happiness simply in serving. Give us noble aspirations and pure satisfaction. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Thou art my God, and I will praise thee.
body: Father, we’re grateful for the tenderness wrapped up in that very name — if you’re a Father, then we’re your children. Give us a trusting heart today, and help us rely on your good ways with us. We don’t even know what we truly need, and sometimes we ask for stones mistaking them for bread. Help us trust ourselves to your wise counsel and fatherly heart, accepting gladly whatever you give, sure that your gifts are always best. Keep our souls at peace, confident that everything works together for our good. Let our words be honest today and our actions upright; give us compassion for people in every condition, and soften our hearts with the sympathy of Jesus. And if any hidden sin still lingers in us, let your forgiveness wash over us until we’re clean, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: If thou seek him, he will be found of thee.
body: Infinite Wisdom, we, your shortsighted children, need your guidance through today. We don’t know what joy or sorrow it may hold, but we believe your grace is enough for whatever comes, so help us truly receive that freely given grace. If sorrow is our lot, let that grace comfort and strengthen us; if joy is ours, let it keep us humble and dependent on you. Amid all the uncertainty of our path, hold our hand and keep us on your road. Help us set aside the restless urge to wander past the boundaries you’ve set, and be content to follow the safe path you mark out. We’re depending on you — you’ve never failed us before, and we trust you today, even though we can’t see the way, because it’s clear to you. Guide us safely, through the one who loved us and gave himself for us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by J. Stewart French, D.D., Bristol, Tenn.

quote: Let the people praise thee, O God.
body: Blessed God, uphold us today by your gracious, all-powerful hand. Give us whatever measure of blessing you see fit, and if disappointment or difficulty awaits us, help us brace ourselves and meet it like someone who trusts that our hardest trials are often blessings in disguise — so that we can always give thanks, sure that all things work together for our good because we love you. Give us holy ideals, and let our daily effort match them. Shine your Spirit’s light into whatever is dark in us, and cleanse us of wrongdoing. Let us be truly sorry for our sins, and strengthened inwardly to do your will. Don’t let today’s sun set without some small kindness done or some word of Christian love spoken, so that everyone we walk beside recognizes we’ve been with Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks.
body: Thessalonians 5:16–23 Create in us a clean heart, God, and renew a right spirit within us. Don’t cast us from your presence, and don’t take your Holy Spirit from us. We entrust to your loving protection everyone we long to pray for — naming them silently before you — and ask that you give them their heart’s desire, as far as you see it’s best, for Jesus’ sake. Bring each of us, Father, to the close of this day in peace and honor. For everyone who loves us far better than we deserve, we thank you, and for their sakes, help us to live rightly today. Grant that we stay steady in this purpose, mastering our desires and emotions by your continual help. Amen.
attribution: compiled and adapted, from a contributor to the collection.

quote: My prayer is unto thee, O Lord.
body: God, our Father, bless us in this moment of spiritual communion with you. We come before you keenly aware of our own unworthiness — we’ve sinned in thought, word, and deed — yet hear us as we turn back to you with penitent hearts. Forgive our sins, restore your peace to us, and give us grace to serve you in a renewed life, for the glory of your name. Thank you for your constant goodness — for provision, protection, redeeming love, sustaining grace, and the promise of a home in heaven. Keep us from the evil within us and around us, from selfish and unkind thoughts, from harsh words, and from failing to do what’s right. Keep us always aware that we belong to Christ, as his disciples, in the love of our Father’s house and the hope of our eternal home, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: compiled and adapted, from a contributor to the collection.

quote: O sing unto the Lord a new song; for he hath done marvellous things.
body: Kind Heavenly Father, we could never presume to address you this way if not for the cross that opened the way for us. In Christ’s name we come, confessing sins too many to name and too serious to fully grasp, seeking your forgiveness and the power of your Spirit to restore us fully to your favor. As we try, in our weakness, to lift our eyes toward you, protect our vision from the pull of the flesh, the temptations of the world, and the deceptions of evil. Let your Spirit govern all our thoughts, words, plans, and relationships today, so that when the day ends, no memory brings regret, but only calm and holy peace. Sanctify the world with your truth, and guide all human effort toward you. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: We thank thee, and praise thy glorious name.
body: Father in heaven, we’re your children, made in your image, redeemed by your Son’s blood, dependent on your grace for everything we enjoy. Our health, happiness, food, and every good gift show your gracious care; give us the strength to honor you for it by loving one another and doing good wherever we can. Come, blessed Savior, and live within us by your Spirit, teaching us your will in everything. We’ve often forgotten you and disobeyed your commands — forgive us, for your name’s sake. As each new day begins, remind us that real success comes only through your favor, and let us honor your name in the ordinary tasks of life. Whatever difficult duty or dangerous temptation we face, help us remember that our strength is found in Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
body: Father in heaven, help us start this new day with you — may its first moments be laid on your altar, refreshed by the dew of sleep. You’ve taught us that prayer rises like incense; may our morning petition reach your holy place. We don’t know what today’s path holds — there may be swollen streams, hidden dangers, or unseen struggles, even after a bright sunrise. We’d choose the easy road, where flowers bloom and birds sing, but we submit our choices to you, since we want your presence most when darkness falls. In loving, prompt obedience to your will, may we find new purpose in our waking hours, and may everyone whose path crosses ours be glad we passed their way. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: We know that all things work together for good.
body: Lord, how slow we are to recognize you when you come in disguise. We know you in robes of light, but not when you’re clothed in clouds. Help us learn your ways, and thank you for everything you do — even when you lead us through the fire of hardship, where you reveal yourself as the one who purifies and delivers. So often you’ve come to us in humble, everyday ways, and we’ve missed you because we weren’t looking there. Like Mary at the tomb, we sometimes mistake you for the gardener instead of the Lord — but may we, like her, keep asking after the one we love, until you reveal yourself to us. Forgive us, Lord, for the times unbelief has turned your blessing into something we couldn’t recognize. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord is my light and my salvation.
body: Heavenly Father, we’re yours, and we want to serve you — thank you for making us your own in Christ, and for the privilege of serving you. Help us serve you today, each in the place your providence has put us, letting our light shine right where we are, with the same mindset as Christ, who though Lord of all didn’t seek to please himself. Make us strong to do right and resist wrong; give us confident, trusting love for you, and warm goodwill toward everyone, especially fellow believers. Forgive our sins, and let us grow more and more into a life devoted to what’s right. Bless the discipline of life to us, and let us care more about learning from it than escaping its discomfort, for Jesus’ sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. M. McPheeters, D.D., Columbia, S.C.

quote: We ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard.
body: Hebrews 2:1–3 Heavenly Father, thank you for every generous gift from your hand — for life, health, friends, and home. Thank you for your protection while we slept, and for this new morning’s call to work, for food and shelter and the peace of this house. Guide us today in all we do, so we do your will in every relationship, staying patient, faithful, considerate, and kind, and not falling into temptation and sin. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him.
body: In the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Thank you, blessed Lord, for the loving care that guarded us through the night and brought us safely to this new morning. Fill our hearts with gratitude expressed not just in words but in lives given over to your service. Help us appreciate every blessing of this life — health, reason, the love of those around us, and above all, your love. Bless our dear ones wherever they are; keep them from harm in body and sin in soul. Be merciful to the sick, the sorrowing, and the dying, granting them peace beyond understanding. Bless your church, and let your kingdom grow. We commend ourselves to you now — watch over us today, keep us from evil, and sanctify us through your indwelling Spirit, for Jesus Christ’s sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Let us lay aside... the sin which doth so easily beset us.
body: Dear Heavenly Father, it’s your hand that opens the gates of morning and draws the curtains of night around us. Thank you for every blessing that enriches our days, the watchful care that shields us from harm, and the strength of body and mind to do our work. Your compassion never fails, and your love has no limit — you care for each of us as though each were your only child. In response to all your love, may we live lives wholly dedicated to you, glorifying you with every affection of our hearts and every work of our hands. May we do nothing you can’t approve, ask for nothing you can’t give, and go nowhere you can’t go with us. Blot out our many failures, strengthen us against every temptation, and let us grow daily closer to our Savior, so that each day brings us nearer home. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. G. Arthur Fry, Pittsburgh, Pa.

quote: If ye forgive... your Father will forgive you.
body: Father, we praise you for the blessings that crown us morning and evening, and the love that stays with us through darkness and light. With humble hearts we confess our sins, asking for the cleansing that comes through the cross and the power that helps us grow into the beauty of Christ’s character. Master, we dedicate ourselves to your service — wherever we are, whatever task is given us, help us be like Christ, touching other lives with blessing: cheering the discouraged, comforting the sorrowful, supplying the needy, and leading lost souls to the Savior. You’ve honored us by calling us to work alongside you; let us give our full strength to it, so that earth becomes more like heaven. Keep us true to the highest ideals, and give us your peace in ever-growing measure. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. E. McCulloch, D.D., Pittsburgh, Pa.

quote: Incline my heart unto thy testimonies.
body: Father, thank you for the gift of life, for a sound body and mind, for a sensitive conscience, a strong will, and the privilege of serving you. Thank you for setting the lonely in families, and for our place in your great family, where you’re our Father. We’re grateful for everything that makes life rich and worth living — the love of parents, siblings, friends, education, and country. Give us the strength to live and serve as we should. Bless our family, our neighborhood, our city, our nation. Give grace to our leaders, wisdom to our teachers, and your blessing on our schools, hospitals, and prisons, that good can come even out of suffering. Keep the nations of the earth at peace. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Faith which worketh by love.
body: Great and eternal God, Creator, Redeemer, and generous giver of every good and perfect gift — we gather as a family to worship you. Breathe true devotion into our hearts, and give us real repentance for our sins. You’ve taught us that only one thing can come between our souls and you — the one thing you hate: sin. We rejoice that we can be freed from it, bearing fruit in holiness and, at the end, everlasting life, trusting your promise that if we confess our sins, you’re faithful to forgive and cleanse us. Give us faith — faith in Jesus as our present, all- sufficient Savior. Give us hope — the anchor that holds steady through life’s storms. Give us love — the perfect love that casts out fear. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The fruit of the Spirit is love.
body: God of infinite love and compassion, who taught us to call you Father and revealed that you pity your children the way a father pities his own — we come before your throne with reverence and humility. We’ve sinned and fallen short of your glory; even when we want to do good, evil is close at hand. Yet, Lord, we’ll never be satisfied until we wake in your likeness. Have mercy on us, and according to your abundant tender mercy, blot out our wrongs. Let Christ live in our hearts through faith, rooted and grounded in love, so we can grasp, with all believers, the full scope of Christ’s love, and be filled with the fullness of God — growing daily into him, bearing the Spirit’s fruit, so that people recognize we’ve been with Jesus. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Marshall P. Talling.

quote: Thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.
body: God, our Heavenly Father, thank you for every gracious gift your love provides. Whatever hardship we face, teach us to submit to your will, and forgive our failures for the sake of the one who atoned for our sins. With hearts softened by your boundless mercy, help us forgive everyone who’s wronged us. For everyone we should remember before you, we ask the blessing they need. Advance your kingdom throughout the world, and by your Spirit make us workers together with you for everyone’s salvation. Give our leaders honesty and competence, and pity everyone facing hardship. Let Christ live in our hearts so fully that we seek to serve rather than be served. Give us strength for our work and our burdens, and when you’re ready for us, call us home to the joy of your eternal presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Lewis W. Burton, D.D., Lexington, Kentucky.

quote: I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
body: 40:1–4 Father, every family in heaven and on earth takes its name from you. Thank you for our own home and hearth, and for the whole human family — we pray today for ourselves and for all our brothers and sisters everywhere. Send us out to our work with willing hearts and ready hands, and equip us and everyone else for the burdens we’ll carry today. Bring us home tonight after a day of honest work, and grant us rest and peaceful sleep. Accept our thanks for your mercy to us and to everyone, and give us grateful hearts besides, in the name and Spirit of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water.
body: Father in heaven and on earth, come and be the center of our family’s love and peace. We differ in what we want, in temperament and taste, and selfishness threatens to spoil our unity — only as you live in us, and we in you, can we find the oneness that brings real happiness and strength. As we go out today to our work and our pleasures, help us keep you and each other in mind. Help each of us set aside self-centered wants, making room for the comfort and good of the whole household, remembering the larger unity of Christian life you’ve planned for us in Jesus. May your fatherhood shape our nation and every nation into one family marked by righteousness and peace. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Yet will I not forget thee.
body: Heavenly Father, with grateful hearts we thank you this morning. You kept us safe through the night; restful sleep has renewed us, and we look ahead to today’s duties with courage. If it weren’t for the assurance that whatever trial or difficulty the coming hours bring, none of it surprises you, we’d hesitate to step into the unknown future. As we part ways to our daily work, let there be no separation from you. Whatever we do for others, let it be done faithfully, as though for you rather than for people. If our work is the ordinary routine of home, full of small irritations, help us stay calm and even-tempered, showing your power at work in us. Don’t let the enemy of our souls gain ground today — you’re stronger than he is; help us stay alert. Give us Christ’s mindset today, unselfish and attentive to others’ needs. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Believe in the Lord your God.
body: Heavenly Father, a new day opens before us — let us step through its gates with gratitude for every mercy of the past, and a song of praise in our hearts. We’re deeply aware of our sin and unworthy of your kindness, and we know how much we depend on you; we ask for your presence with us today. Don’t let us shirk any duty or complain about any trial — keep us gentle and hopeful, kind in word and thought, and save us from careless, unguarded moments. We pray for the people we love, and for those who don’t love us — for strangers, the poor, the sick, the lonely, and the wayward. Be present with everyone laboring in your name worldwide, and send out more workers. Bless children everywhere and the helpless elderly. Let wars end, and let us serve you today so faithfully that we rest tonight fully aware of your presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake.
body: Almighty God, our Heavenly Father, as we begin another day, we humbly seek you as our guide, protector, and merciful Savior. All our strength comes from you; your wisdom gives us light and truth, your presence gives us joy and comfort. We don’t know what snares, trials, or burdens today may bring — make us wise enough to see where temptation lies and strong enough to resist it. Let us be brave and patient under trial, cheerful under burdens, and quick to recognize sin in our own hearts. Breathe into us a spirit of fervent prayer and complete trust, and help us notice each other’s needs, so that by helpful word and deed, someone finds it easier to stay strong and faithful because of us. Let this day not pass without some good done in the Master’s name. Forgive all our sins, Father, and help us forgive one another as Christ commanded. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: To know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge.
body: Father in heaven, we praise you, the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the great Shepherd who, when we like sheep had all gone astray, laid on him the weight of all our wrongdoing. Forgive our sins, we ask, in his name. Show us how much we truly need you — not only for rescue, but for daily grace and guidance. Lead us into the green pastures of your love, and give us to drink from the water of everlasting life. Make the path of duty and privilege clear before us, and help us walk it so it becomes, for us, a path that shines brighter and brighter until full day. Help us be kind, tender-hearted, and honest with others, filled with the Spirit’s power so we’re faithful witnesses for Christ — living so well that when the Chief Shepherd appears, we receive the crown of life that never fades. For Christ’s sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Russell Cecil, D.D., Richmond, Virginia.

quote: O sing unto the Lord a new song; sing unto the Lord, all the earth.
body: Father of us all, thank you for life, and that we’re alive to see it now — that our eyes have opened to today’s beauty, and our hands are full of today’s work. We don’t despise the past whose labors we’ve inherited; its mistakes warn us, its successes teach us, its sacrifices inspire us, and we owe an endless debt to its brave souls. We’re grateful for the world’s moral leaders — for the trailblazers of liberty, the voices who value people over gold and the soul of a child over any city’s grandeur. We’re grateful for friends whose faith in us makes us better, for children who call us by the holiest name we’ll ever hear, for tasks we’re unworthy of yet grateful for, and for Jesus of Nazareth, your Son and our only Savior, in whose name we pray. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Incline your heart unto the Lord God of Israel.
body: Heavenly Father, accept our morning prayer and praise. We praise you for bringing us safely to the start of another day, for preserving us throughout our lives, for every mercy despite our repeated failures — and especially for Jesus Christ our Savior, through whom come all our grace and hope. Give us the grace, amid worldly cares, never to forget you, always aware that we’re walking in your sight. Help us subdue unholy desires and live rightly and faithfully in this present world. Keep us from laziness in matters of soul and body, diligent in our work and fervent in spirit, serving the Lord. Comfort and help the poor and the suffering, and move us to do good to everyone. Spread the knowledge of your Word, and make your Church a force for true religion everywhere. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Lord, increase our faith.
body: Father in heaven, it’s right that we acknowledge you every day — you never forget us. Teach us to keep you always before our eyes. Our reasons for thanksgiving are new every morning; give us grateful hearts. Keep us from sin, cleanse us of its stain, and save us from its guilt; grant us real repentance, and help us overcome evil with good. Give us eyes to see and hearts to understand, so we value our time and recognize our opportunities. Help us love you above all and our neighbors as ourselves. Give us our daily bread, and enough to share with those who lack. Keep our eyes on the harvest fields and the Lord of the Harvest, who sends the workers we need — give us some part in that labor. Hasten your kingdom, and let our days end in peace, dwelling in your house forever. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: If thou canst believe, all things are possible.
body: Father, we bless you for the privilege, through Jesus our Lord, of calling you Father. This new day, we put our hands in yours and ask you to lead us. The future is dark to us except where it’s lit by the hope of your presence going with us — but you already know every temptation, danger, and opportunity that lies ahead. Remembering how you led your servants of old to victory over every weakness and enemy, we’re encouraged to trust you. Make each of us a help to Christ’s advancing kingdom today. Bring our neighbors to mind, and make our duty to them clear; let our sympathy reach out to everyone sorrowing on earth, and help our efforts spread the gospel that’s sweetened our own lives and filled our hearts with hope. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.
body: Heavenly Father, as we close our eyes tonight, we open our hearts to you. You know us completely — our deepest thoughts, ambitions, and secret ways are all open before you; we can’t deceive you, so keep us from deceiving others or ourselves. Let us be sincere, without pretense, our lives all of one piece, like Christ’s seamless garment — spare us the folly of a divided life, reverent on the day of worship but hard and selfish on ordinary days. Make us thoughtful toward those who serve us and faithful to those we serve, and let our daily work be devoted to you, so that not just its results but the labor itself — of hand, heart, and mind — serves your kingdom. Make all our friendships, books, rest, love, laughter, and service sacred to you, that yours may be the glory, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Herbert Welch, D.D., LL.D.

quote: The love of God is shed abroad in our hearts.
body: Living and loving God, our Father and Friend, you created everything in wisdom, for your own pleasure. To know you is life; to serve you is freedom; to praise you is our greatest joy. As you made us in your image, remake us today in the likeness of Christ, the unchanging light of life and unfailing source of strength. Help us accept him again with childlike faith and follow faithfully in his steps — in him may our sins be forgiven, our affections purified, our wills brought into line, and our work blessed. Sanctify our worship at home and in church through your indwelling Spirit, and make our lives useful and joyful, for the sake of the one who taught us to pray: “Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name...” Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
body: Heavenly Father, give us renewed strength to overcome all our faults, a renewed spirit of goodwill toward everyone, and a firmer faith in you and in every promise of your Word. Help us follow the good shepherd who leads us to green pastures and still waters, restores our souls, and walks with us even through the darkest valley, fearless because he’s with us. Prepare a table for us even amid our troubles, and let goodness and mercy follow us all our days, that we may dwell in your house forever. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Without faith it is impossible to please God.
body: Father in heaven, with praise on our lips and gratitude in our hearts, we, your children, worship you. You’ve fed us from your hand, clothed us by your generosity, and kept us safe day and night under the shelter of your love — for all our poor service, we’ve received everything freely from you. Forgive our ingratitude, we ask, and cast away the memory of our sins, which we sincerely repent of. Stir up in us a compelling desire to love you above everything and do your will in every part of our lives. Give us grace to show, in word, thought, and deed, that we’ve been with Christ and learned from him. Let your kingdom come, in some measure, through our own lives, so your name is glorified, and by your indwelling Spirit, prepare us for your service until you bring us home, for Jesus Christ’s sake. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John Gribbel, Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink.
body: 6:25–26 Almighty God, Creator, Sustainer, and gracious Ruler of the universe — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit — we praise your great name, not only for your majesty but for your divine love and compassion. Thank you for your goodness and every blessing of life, and we humbly ask you to forgive our sins, strengthen our faith, and help us love and serve you better. We pray for peace in the world, for the spread of the gospel, and for the salvation of humanity. Graciously give us, in this life, food, shelter, friends, and happiness, and in the next, life everlasting, for the sake of your beloved Son. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way that thou shalt go.
body: Father in heaven, we turn our hearts to you as the source of life, truth, and love. We don’t claim your constant generosity because we’ve earned it, but in Christ’s name, we seek your favor anyway. Give us our daily portion today — food for the body, nourishment for the mind, and above all, the Bread of Life to strengthen our hearts and purify our souls. Teach us to love others as you love us, forgiving those who wrong us and helping those in need. Don’t let temptation grow greater than we can bear, and give us the grace to do our appointed work with a cheerful heart. When night falls, let us feel your presence, as one who has walked with us all day. In your name we pray. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Prof. Edward B. Pollard, D.D., Chester, Pa.

quote: Let your requests be made known unto God.
body: Father in heaven, we come to you glad and grateful for our dependence on you. Thank you for the blessings of the night — restful sleep, safety from harm, and renewed strength with this new day. We want to begin today with you, receiving your blessing before we step onto its untried paths. Stay with us through every hour, so that amid our busy duties we’re not caught off guard by sudden temptation and fall. Help us do our duty well, without shame over neglected or careless work. Give us a spirit of friendship and a word of encouragement to offer, so our lives radiate joy, leaving hope and happiness in our wake. And when life’s evening comes, gather us home through the blood of the everlasting covenant, into your arms, fearless and unashamed. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow-citizens with the saints.
body: Ephesians 2:19–22 Dear Father, the privileges we have are almost too great to grasp — to come to you, King of kings, at any time and place, invited to ask, seek, and knock, with the assurance that everyone who asks receives. For these priceless privileges, we thank you. Today lies ahead of us, and soon it will be behind us forever — we only get to live through it once. Father, cleanse us of all sin through Christ’s sacrifice, and make our bodies temples of your Spirit. Use us so we leave nothing undone that we should do, and do nothing we should have left undone. Keep us happy in you, and give us an unwavering faith. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him.
body: God and Father of us all, you watch over your children through every joy and sorrow — blessed God forever. You’re the light of the living, the refuge of the dying, and our eternal home. You’ve placed us in families and joined the hearts that make the happiest homes, and you’ve led us graciously through the past — our yesterdays shine with your mercies, guiding us safely through both seen and unseen dangers. On calm days you’ve carried us gently, and when trouble rises, we trust it only draws us closer to you, into deeper fellowship with the one truly lasting world — the spiritual one. Comfort the mourners; walk with them through life’s journey, and strengthen them as only you can. You’re the Lord of life and death — if we’re joined to you by living faith, nothing can separate us from your gracious guidance. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: He heareth the prayer of the righteous.
body: Gracious and loving Father, how tenderly you’ve guarded and guided us — we gratefully acknowledge your goodness. We long for closer fellowship with you; show us the path you’ve marked out for us in your wisdom. The climb is hard — give us strength for life’s tasks and temptations, and grant us trusting calm where the way ahead is unclear. Keep us steady amid turmoil, and patient in hardship. Let the redeeming passion of Jesus Christ become so real to us that we delight in humble service to you and love for others. Make us willing to take on hard tasks when we sense it’s your will. We long to know the truth — reward us with insight that builds and blesses us. We pray for anyone in deep affliction; teach us to bring comfort to the sad, hope to the discouraged, and peace to the troubled. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: He that trusteth in the Lord, mercy shall compass him about.
body: Father, in whom we live and move and exist, thank you for your care, our home, our parents, and our friends. Thank you for the joy of salvation, health of body, vigor of mind, and the delight of good company. Thank you for Jesus Christ, his sacrifice for us, and the promise of eternal life through faith in him. Teach us to appreciate your boundless care and constant watchfulness, and show us what you’d have us do. Teach us to be kind and helpful to one another, bringing joy into others’ lives. Give us your Holy Spirit, so we understand your Word and how to live it out. Help us stay watchful in prayer amid temptation, hating evil and holding only to what’s good. Strengthen us in hardship, and protect us from the snares that come with prosperity. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Let the poor and needy praise thy name.
body: Father in heaven, we kneel together to thank you for your goodness and mercy, so evident in our lives. Your good gifts have never failed, morning or evening — even when we’ve forgotten you in the busyness of work and play, you’ve kept watching over us to bless and protect us. Keep us from unholy desires, and inspire in us love for you, for others, and for good work. Open doors of opportunity so we can honor your name each day. Give us the privilege of constant fellowship with you, so we’re confident of your nearness and your interest in our lives. Forgive everything that has marred our souls — we’re ashamed of it, and turn from it in real repentance, grateful that forgiveness and cleansing are found in Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by W. Courtland Robinson, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Make confession unto the Lord God of your fathers.
body: Father in heaven, we bow before you grateful for the night’s care and this new day’s light and hope. Let us begin it in the joy of forgiven sin, and end it with souls unstained by willful wrongdoing. Give us wisdom through your indwelling Spirit, so today’s choices are right, and keep us from every temptation and danger. Fill us with love — for you, your kingdom, and for others. Let your presence today rest on everyone connected to our lives; give them every blessing we ask for ourselves, and keep from sin and harm everyone dear to us. Have mercy on your people everywhere, build up a holy Church across the world, and strengthen those witnessing for Christ in hard places. Minister to the poor, the sick, the imprisoned, and the oppressed. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.
body: God, our Heavenly Father, who showed your love by sending your Son Jesus Christ to be our Redeemer — help us live today, and every day, in gratitude for what you’ve done and are doing for us. In every temptation and duty, teach us to seek your sufficient grace, and to actually use it, so we don’t fall into sin or fail to do the work you’ve given us. Help us remember that just as Christ has enlightened us, we’re meant to be light to the world. Keep us from denying you through our lives even while we profess you with our lips, and from harming others through our inconsistency. Increase our faith, hope, and love, and use us as you will, wherever and whenever, for your glory and the world’s salvation. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Bishop Joseph M. Francis, D.D., Indianapolis, Indiana.

quote: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.
body: Merciful God, our Father, thank you for health, life, and every good gift. You made us in your image, gifted with the capacity to think and reason. We recognize your right to rule over us, and ask to be kept honest and right before you. Give us grace for today’s duties, and make us kind toward everyone we meet. Support your people everywhere facing hardship, and draw the world to yourself. Show mercy to the poor and unfortunate, and rescue people from the sins that trap them. For ourselves, our loved ones, our community, and our nation, we offer this humble prayer, asking every blessing you see we need, through the merit of Jesus Christ, our beloved Savior. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The prayer of faith shall save the sick.
body: Father in heaven, we kneel in this home you’ve given us and blessed us with. As we enjoy the good things of this earthly home, help us not forget the better home you’ve prepared for those who love you, where we’ll one day live with you and with loved ones gone before. Provide our daily bread today, and feed not just our bodies but our souls with the bread of life, Jesus Christ. Keep our feet from evil paths, and our lips from unkind or unclean words; create clean hearts within us, since life flows from the heart, and let whatever our hands find to do be done wholeheartedly, as for you. Touch every sick and troubled person with your healing grace, and let it be enough for them. Shelter everyone we love under your protection, and lead us all along the good and perfect way. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Then will I hear from heaven, and forgive their sins.
body: Almighty God, our Heavenly Father, thank you for the way opened to you through the torn veil of Christ’s own body, for the power of his precious blood to cleanse us from all sin, and for the promised help of the Spirit when we don’t know how to pray. Thank you for the assurance that you hear us and delight to answer prayers that align with your will. We bless you for your indescribable gift, the sacrifice of Christ, and the grace so freely given to sinful people. Accept the devotion of our hearts, the surrender of our wills, and help us stay true to you in every circumstance. Deliver us in temptation, keep our steps steady, and help us not sin against you. Help us see sin as our real enemy, and fill us with Christ’s spirit, so our words and actions reveal his life in us and constantly glorify you. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.
body: Gracious Father in heaven, welcome us as a family into your presence, that we may worship you in spirit and truth. Accept our grateful praise for all you are and all you’ve done for us and everyone else, especially for our redemption through your Son, Jesus Christ. Father, reveal our sins and faults so we can repent and turn from them, and forgive us, cleansing us of all wrongdoing. Let your Holy Spirit live in us today, restraining us from wrong and guiding us into truth and peace. Guard our weakest points of character — keep us from vanity, pride, unkind thoughts, and harsh words. Help us love you fully and love one another warmly, serving you by serving others, and grant us at last a home with you in heaven, through Christ our Savior. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Jesse Thompson Whitley, D.D., Norfolk, Virginia.

quote: Let them praise thy great and terrible name.
body: Dear Lord and Master, you’ve set each family apart and deal with each of us according to our faithfulness. We humbly ask forgiveness for past mistakes and your guidance for the days ahead — we truly need you every hour, since without your guidance we’d be led astray or fall into danger. Guard us from hidden dangers, seen and unseen. We put our trials, needs, and troubles into your hands, asking you to deal with us as with little children — we have no fear of you, Almighty Father, because we’re assured of your love. Watch over our work and help us stay honest and fair in it, guiding us to always do what’s right in your sight. Lead us safely through life, and at last give us the eternal life we long for more than any treasure. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Bless the Lord, O my soul.
body: God, our Heavenly Father, through your mercy we’ve come to the saving knowledge of Jesus Christ, and by your goodness we begin another day’s duties. Thank you for your loving kindness, and let us show forth your praise today in word and life. Banish doubt from our minds and shadow from our souls, and help us feel your presence in everything we do. Give us grace to think what’s right and courage to speak what advances your kingdom. Keep our loved ones safe in body and soul, defended from harm and evil thought. Keep your Church faithful, and let the dedicated work of Christians everywhere bring the whole world to Jesus Christ. And when our brief life on earth is done, may we, with everyone we love, enter into eternal praise in your presence. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Let us draw near with a pure heart in full assurance of faith.
body: Our God and Father, we come to you with grateful hearts for all your mercy and goodness. We know we’re unworthy of even your smallest favor — we have nothing to recommend us to you except our own weakness and need — but we’re glad that, despite our unworthiness, you invite us to come and tell you everything in our hearts. We confess our sins and ask your forgiveness; we plead for your grace and the strength only you can give for every part of life. Draw us nearer to yourself; let us stay conscious of your presence and lifted by the assurance of your guidance. Make the nobler life of the Spirit more real to us each day, filling our thoughts and helping us overcome every temptation, so that our lives become a blessing to others until you receive us to yourself. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by A. Judson Rowland, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: They that know thy name will put their trust in thee.
body: God, you’re our Father and our Mother too, and there’s no place we can go beyond the reach of your tireless love. Since our birth you’ve cared for us as if we were your only child, following us still with countless gentle persuasions and infinite care. Let your goodness lead us to deeper devotion and braver effort to extend your kingdom. May we prove our love for you, whom we haven’t seen, through selfless service to the people right in front of us. Save us from selfishness, self-righteousness, and pride, and all narrow-mindedness. Help us make Christ visible to those who haven’t yet seen him, remembering the one who came not to be served but to serve, giving his life so we could live with Christlike courage and sacrifice. Hear us, Father, on behalf of all people, and bring an end to war throughout the world. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Dillon Bronson, D.D., Boston, Mass.

quote: The living shall praise thee.
body: Heavenly Father, thank you for last night’s restful sleep, for sparing us to see another day, for our loved ones and this family altar, and for the gift of your Son Jesus Christ, with his love and self-sacrifice. We sincerely repent of our wrongdoing — pardon our sins, and give us a forgiving spirit. Help us trust your Word, finding in it medicine for the mind and food for the soul. We pray for our country and for leaders everywhere. Bless the poor, the sick, the dying, the grieving, and everyone in distress, and plead for anyone treated unjustly, until justice flows like a river. Reward the preaching of your gospel everywhere, and pour out your Spirit on our church until all people, great and small, know you. To you we give the glory forever. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Capt. (Rev.) H. S. Mullowney, M.A.

quote: He shall call upon me, and I will answer him.
body: Loving Father, help us grasp what a privilege it is to come directly into your presence, through your Son’s relationship as our Savior and Elder Brother, truly your children. Help us call you “our Father” today, and know that your loving heart turns toward us the way a parent’s heart turns toward a child — may this relationship grow more precious every day. As we take up today’s duties, let us shelter under the promises of Psalm 91, fulfilled for us and our loved ones. Let us be a help to someone who needs us today, careful of our example, walking in a way others can safely follow. Through faith in Jesus Christ, may we be clothed in his righteousness. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble.
body: Almighty God, our Heavenly Father, bless this family and household, and everyone dear to them, wherever they are — bless them with every good gift, both practical and spiritual. Bless them in their work and their rest, their going out and coming in, and everything they set their hand to. But above all, bless them spiritually — deepen their faith, nourish them with goodness, and in your great mercy keep them close to you always. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: I prayed unto the Lord my God, and made my confession.
body: Everliving, everloving God, our Heavenly Father, we bless you for setting the human race in families, for our growth and mutual influence. This morning we bless your name for calling us into this family now gathered in prayer. Help us recognize our duty to you, to each other, and to our community. Keep us from sin today as we do our work, watch over us, and guard us from danger. Teach us to live unselfishly with each other in all the small things of home life. As parents, siblings, and family, help us fulfill our roles with the example of our Elder Brother always before us. Prosper each one’s work, and above all, give our family the lasting richness of a real, helpful faith in our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by L. B. Wolf, D.D., Baltimore, Maryland.

quote: Men ought always to pray, and not to faint.
body: Heavenly Father, we come to you in humble worship this morning, thankful for your loving care while we slept and for a night of rest. Refreshed in body and mind, we’ve come to see a new day — Lord, stay with us still. We need you always; protect us from harm, guide us through today’s duties, deliver us from evil, and make us strong to do your will. Remember with your blessing all our loved ones, even those far away, since you’re present everywhere. Bless your work in the world — give great grace to ministers and Christian workers everywhere, that your name would be glorified through their efforts. Now we commit ourselves and our loved ones to your care; forgive our sins, and guide us by your Spirit today, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Douglas Laing.

quote: The Lord knoweth them that trust him.
body: Heavenly Father, we lift our hearts in adoring praise for your love and grace made known to us in Jesus Christ our Savior, who died for our sins. Thank you for your Word, able to make us wise for salvation — help us read it and truly take it to heart. Thank you for the Holy Spirit, who reveals Christ to us, guides us into truth, and comforts us all our lives; help us recognize him in everything we think, say, and do, and never grieve him, but follow him and feel his presence. We need you in life’s small things as much as its big ones — help us control our words, and live each day expecting our Lord’s return, ready when he comes. Bless every family on earth. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord loveth the righteous.
body: Lord our God, we come before you in the name of Jesus Christ, your Son, our Savior. Give us a joyful sense of being accepted in him, and let his Spirit in us cry out, “Father.” We want to know you more and more — reveal yourself to us through your Word and through the Spirit of Jesus. We want to love you; show us your love, and we’ll trust and serve you in everything we think, say, and do. Loving and serving you, we’ll love and serve everyone else too, as part of God’s great family on earth, seeking each other’s good and so fulfilling the law of Christ. Work out your will and purpose in us every day, preparing us to meet you and be filled with you, made your instruments for higher and richer service through eternity. We ask this not just for ourselves, but for everyone. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
body: 103:8–13 Almighty God and gracious Father, hear our prayer today. Bless us with health and happiness, sound minds, light hearts, clear vision of our duties, and above all, sound judgment in everything. Guard our inexperience, keep us from self- conceit, and help us become like children so we grow truly wise — gentle so we grow truly strong, humble so we grow closer to you. Prepare us to live our lives honorably, so that we may serve you well in this world. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: My peace I give unto you.
body: Giver of every good and perfect gift, in whose unfailing love we live and move and exist, without whom we’d truly be poor — help us see your abundant goodness more clearly, and as you’ve made us rich in blessing, make us equally rich in gratitude. We praise you for the everyday revelations of your love we too easily take for granted — sunrise and sunset, stars, clouds, wind, and passing seasons; the outer light we walk safely in, and the inner light that assures us of our oneness with you. Help us understand every blessing as an expression of your love. Thank you for our friends, and for the privilege of counting ourselves friends of Jesus Christ; help us understand the high calling that friendship with him brings. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Ye believe in God, believe also in me.
body: Almighty God, in whom we live and move and exist, we adore you as the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whose name we bring our worship, thanksgiving, and requests. Thank you for the gift of your Son, through whom we’re redeemed, and in whose name we ask forgiveness for all our sins. Keep us today in joy, health, and safety from whatever dangers surround us, and let us walk daily in reverence, following the one who called us into his kingdom. Free us from envy, fear, and temptation; grant us what’s truly good, and forgive our sins against you. Deliver us from whatever divides people from each other and causes them to stumble from the truth. Free us from selfishness, and give us willingness to carry one another’s burdens. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: My God, unto thee will I pray.
body: Holy Father, thank you for the privilege of prayer — it’s a mark of your amazing goodness that we’re allowed to pray, and of your infinite wisdom that our prayers are answered. We’re grateful for life, health, and every blessing, and above all, for the Savior. Thinking of your gracious gifts, our hearts echo the words of Scripture: thanks be to God for his indescribable gift. We lay ourselves before you, Holy One — you alone are God, and there’s no other. Bless our home, and guide us to make it what you’d have it be. Make our relationships with each other holy, becoming everything you’ve planned for our lives. Bless every other family too, our neighbors, our friends, and even the stranger far away — hear us on their behalf, and give them every good thing we’d ask for ourselves. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord is worthy to be praised.
body: You who are the same yesterday, today, and forever — as we look back over our lives, how many different glimpses of you we’ve had. Some days we’ve been sure of your infinite kindness; other days we’ve groaned in bitterness. On bright mornings our hearts have sung despite themselves, and on dark nights they’ve sunk into despair — yet you’re the same God, always merciful, never treating us as our sins deserve. Father, we dare to believe that what Jesus was, you are — he unveiled you for us. As tempted, defeated people trusted him and weren’t let down, as scorned people trusted him and found him faithful, as children reached for him without hesitation, so may the children of our homes and hearts reach for you, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
body: Lord, our Lord, how excellent is your name in all the earth — your glory set above the heavens, gracious in every act. You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing. Accept our worship and thanks. We confess our unworthiness and unfaithfulness, and humbly ask your fatherly forgiveness. We bring before you the needs of a lost and struggling world — pour out your Holy Spirit on all people, deepening spiritual life and transforming those without hope into the likeness of your Son. Remember this family in your mercy, that it may be a household of faith and a home you delight to dwell in, and when you gather your treasured ones, may our whole family be counted among them, saved by grace. Answer us not according to what we deserve, but according to your abundant mercy. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
body: Father, the night has brought us renewal, strength, rest, and hope, and the day opens before us with its opportunities, tasks, and perhaps its trials too. Thank you for restoring our strength and courage while we slept; we trustingly ask for guidance in whatever today brings. We seek direction that sets us on the right path, wisdom to choose rightly in every situation, and integrity that keeps us loyal to the truth. Don’t let any burden exceed our strength, and if today brings many trials, give us patience, self-control, and steady judgment. Let us lose no faith in others, and no confidence in you. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: The Lord hath made known his salvation.
body: Almighty God and Heavenly Father, who through your Son sanctified the bonds of marriage and family — we thank you warmly for your loving care over our whole lives to this day. We praise you for every happiness, for the affection and sympathy we share with each other, and even for the sorrow you’ve allowed to shape us. Continue your goodness toward us. Give us grace to do our daily duties faithfully, as parents, children, church members, and citizens. Forgive our failures, and give us the kind of sorrow that leads to real repentance. Comfort the distressed, bless the clergy and everyone serving your kingdom, and draw the nations to yourself. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: His faith is counted for righteousness.
body: Almighty Father, Shepherd of our souls, let your face shine on us. Thank you that we can approach your mercy freely — not on our own merit, but through Christ, your beloved Son, crucified for us, who bore our sins and by whose wounds we’re healed. Let your blessing rest on this family circle; help us keep gratitude and devotion burning like a flame. Give us grace to overcome evil in temptation, courage in adversity, and humility in prosperity. Help us live as though always in your sight, doing your will cheerfully. Give wisdom and integrity to everyone in authority over us, that they might govern justly and mercifully. Bless especially this household under this roof, that we might live up to your gracious hopes for us. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
body: We praise you, Lord our King, as we come before you through the merit of Jesus Christ, who redeemed us from sin by his cross and precious blood. We humbly ask you, merciful Father, to pardon our offenses against your law, to create in us a clean heart and right spirit, and to make our words and thoughts pleasing in your sight, our Rock and Redeemer. We bless your holy name for your constant, abundant goodness — we owe you every earthly blessing and every opportunity for usefulness and happiness. Help us, by your Spirit, use these gifts worthily. Be compassionate toward everyone suffering, sorrowing, or struggling with sin — comfort the aged, guide the young, and give wisdom to all who teach. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: O praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people.
body: Almighty God, our Father, accept whatever devotion and worship we, with all our limitations, can bring you. You know that some of us, however willing, can’t grasp you according to accepted standards, and that even your most devoted children often misunderstand you — the best of us see you only dimly, as in a clouded mirror. So we pray you’ll save us all from spiritual pride, and help us guide each other toward the light. Save us from contempt toward those who see differently than we do, and save those of us who see little from judging those who see more. You’ve never forced anyone to acknowledge you, but through your patient providence you’re drawing everyone to yourself — may we, your children, do the same. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Faithful is he that calleth you.
body: God, our hope is in you. We’re in a valley of darkness, but looking up, we see the light of your glory on the hills above, and that vision drives away our fear and fills us with hope. Fill our hearts with a longing for you greater than the watchman’s longing for morning, and give us, through Jesus Christ, a sense of your presence that stays constantly real to us. Give us strength for our work, and let us do it all as though in your sight, for your glory. Make the path of duty clear to us; deepen our faith, hope, and love, and strengthen every worthy purpose in us, making us a blessing to others. Keep us from any mistake in word or deed that would bring shame on your name. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: As Jesus prayed, the heavens were opened.
body: Lord our Heavenly Father, as you’ve graciously spared us to see another morning’s light, accept our glad thanks for this and all your countless mercies. Forgive us wherever we’ve grieved you in the past, and grant us whatever benefits of body, mind, and spirit you see fit for today. Show us your will, and let it become our pleasure. Give us the kind of faith that meets every test successfully, the patience, courage, and joy of those who know your love. Let your blessings to us become, through us, gifts to the world. Remember our loved ones in their particular needs; comfort the afflicted, and bless everyone who labors. Bring salvation, through your Church, to our nation and all people, and hasten the day when evil is done away with. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John Edward Bushnell, D.D.

quote: I praise and extol the King of heaven.
body: God, our Father, we turn to you with this morning’s light, thankful for your mercies and trusting your care. Thank you for the night’s rest and today’s fresh provision, for renewed strength and the chance to serve, for the bonds of family and the comfort of your Word. Help us bear each other’s burdens today and serve you by serving others. Give us grace for today’s duties, and let the spirit of our work reflect our faith. We especially commend to you our loved ones who are far away — though we can’t see them, we’re glad your eye watches over them. May our church be a true family of faith. Bless our nation, that it may uphold righteousness, and bless everyone laboring for the poor and suffering. Be with missionaries proclaiming your love in distant lands, and keep us, Father, through this day, bringing us to its close in peace. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?
body: Grant rest to the weary, dear Lord, and comfort to the sorrowing; shelter to the homeless, and pillow the head of every sufferer on your everlasting arms. Gather the lonely who need you into that same shelter, and let the light of your presence shine on them, so that even in their darkness they see your face and find the peace that belongs to your people. We ask it for the sake of Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by Rev. Henry C. Stone, Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: Do ye now believe?
body: Father, God, we know you through Jesus Christ our Lord, and we praise you for every act of loving kindness and tender mercy. Assured that you’ll never leave or forsake us, we begin the duties of a new day, lifting our eyes to the hills from which our help comes. Direct us in every path we should take, given our responsibilities and opportunities — help us earn our bread honestly, but not so busily that we miss you passing by. Let us live this day before you in reverence, quietness, love, and usefulness. Remember our loved ones everywhere, and bless everyone we should pray for — the sick, the suffering, the sinful — have mercy and meet their needs. Bless our nation through every crisis, giving wisdom to our leaders, and bless the Church of Jesus Christ, its missionaries and ministers. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: Great is thy faithfulness.
body: May we never forget to be thankful to you, our Father — you load us daily with blessings, constantly planning for our good, and yet we’re so often indifferent to your kindness. Our prayers get answered, but we forget to say thank you. Make us more mindful of you, our dependence on you, and your readiness to meet every need. Let us not just speak our gratitude but live it, showing our love for you through our actions. Be present in our home; teach us to trust you, listen to your Word, and do your will, finding real joy in serving you. When doubt disturbs us, give us a vision of you that drives away our distress, and don’t let us darken anyone else’s day with doubting words. Forgive our sins, and make us more earnest in prayer, giving, and service, so our home becomes a source of blessing to everyone near and far. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer by John T. Faris, D.D., Philadelphia, Pa.

quote: If we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us.
body: Father, we bow before you in reverence, thankful for every blessing of life, knowing you’re the giver of every good and perfect gift. We pray that every member of this household would recognize that God has a purpose for each individual life, and that our highest ambition would be to know and do what you ask of us. Let your Holy Spirit stay with us and guide everything we do, and let your evident love for us move us to serve and honor you, our Father. Dear Lord, we commit ourselves, everything we have and are, into your loving care — bless us, keep us, guide us, forgive our sins, and at last bring us home to yourself with all the redeemed. Amen.
attribution: adapted from a prayer submitted from a contributor to the collection.

quote: I thank thee, and praise thee, O Lord of heaven.
body: Father, thank you for your gracious care, new every morning and continuing every evening — for life and health, food and shelter, and your presence that blesses every human relationship. Let us spend this day as though in your sight; keep us pure in heart and clean in life, strong in temptation, brave in danger, patient in trial, and faithful in every trust. Keep the light of our home altar burning bright. Guard our lips from unkind words, our hearts from selfish thoughts, and our hands, so we help one another.
